chapters.title: Chapter 1201. They Communicate With More Lethal Clarity Than Most Elite Units
paragraphs: The fight that followed did not merely continue; it escalated into something primal, a grinding war of attrition that stretched the very fabric of the corridor.
This was no longer a series of exchanges; it was a continuous, overlapping storm of violence where magic and steel became indistinguishable from one another.
Valentina became a living conduit for the arcane. Her grimoire screamed as she maintained a relentless barrage of multi-elemental spellwork, each incantation overlapping the last.
FWOOSH! CRACKLE! SHHHH!
Fireballs spiraled through air frozen solid by frost lances, creating a chaotic weather system of destruction that forced Xerollion to constantly shift his magical defenses.

Beneath this celestial chaos, Morwenna moved like a shadow given lethal intent. She flowed between the explosive bursts of magic, using the momentary blindness caused by Valentina’s flashes to close the distance, landing precise, vicious strikes that sought every gap in his guard.
For the first time that day, Xerollion felt the genuine sting of complication. The mathematical certainty of his victory was being eroded by their combined skill.
Several of Morwenna’s strikes found their mark, carving shallow red furrows across his shoulders and ribs.
SQUELCH. SLICE.

Valentina’s spells weren’t just glancing blows either; molten bolts scorched through his robes, searing flesh with the smell of burnt hair and copper. But every time a wound opened, his Infinite Regeneration roared to life.
The flesh knitted back together with an unnatural, wet sound, SHLIP SHLIP, sealing the damage before the blood could even cool.
The pattern repeated with deadly, exhausting precision for several agonizing minutes. Neither woman would yield; neither would break rhythm.
They were two gears in a single, devastating machine.
’They are learning,’ Xerollion realized, his mind racing to recalibrate. ’They aren’t just attacking; they are studying my defensive patterns.’
’They are looking for the lag in my adaptation.’
Valentina sensed the opening.
"Now, Morwenna!" she cried out, her voice cracking with magical strain.
Valentina called down a lance of pure white lightning from the vaulted ceiling.
KRA KOOOOOM!
Halfway through its flight, she twisted the spell with a violent flick of her wrist, splitting the bolt into three separate, writhing serpents of electricity.
ZZZZZT ZZZZZT ZZZZZT!
Xerollion was forced into a desperate dance, weaving between three lethal paths of ionized air. The moment his attention fractured, the moment his telekinetic focus split three ways, Morwenna struck.
She drove in with a thrust aimed with surgical accuracy directly at the soft gap beneath his ribs.
WHOOSH.
Xerollion twisted at the last possible millisecond, but he was too late to avoid the steel entirely. The blade bit deep into the outside of his hip.
CRUNCH.

The sound of metal grinding against bone echoed off the walls. A thick rivulet of crimson blood sprayed across the stone floor before his flesh sealed itself shut in a grotesque display of supernatural healing.

Valentina saw the blood hit the floor and pressed the advantage mercilessly. She abandoned the wide, theatrical castings, shifting to something far more terrifying: compressed, high-velocity fire bolts.
POP POP POP POP!

Each bolt arrived barely half a second after the last, a rapid fire staccato of heat that forced Xerollion to commit every ounce of his telekinetic energy to deflection. He couldn’t attack; he could only survive.
THUD. THUD. THUD.
Morwenna exploited this lockdown. Using the cover of Valentina’s infernal barrage, she circled wide, her boots silent on the blood-slicked stone.
She came at him from an angle that forced Xerollion to twist his entire torso just to keep her in his peripheral vision. Then she unleashed the killing combination.
SHING SHING!
Her blade flashed twice in terrifying succession. The first was a vicious diagonal slash aimed high at his exposed shoulder, meant to force his guard up and his weight onto his back foot.
The second followed immediately a low, brutal cut aimed directly at the hinge of his knee.
It was the classic ’High Low’ gambit: a trap designed to force a defender to commit their weight in two opposite directions simultaneously.
In that split second, he would either have to protect his throat and lose his leg or protect his knee and expose his neck to the killing blow.

Xerollion read the gambit. His mind, operating at a processing speed that made the world appear to move in slow motion, detected the micro shift in Morwenna’s center of gravity before her blade had even finished its ascent.
WHIP SHING!
The steel whistled through empty air where his shoulder and knee had been a millisecond before. He didn’t just dodge; he exploited the momentum of her own attack.

Pivoting on the ball of one foot with the fluid grace of a dancer and the lethal intent of a predator, he spun into her guard. His palm shot forward—not a punch, but a focused, telekinetically enhanced strike.
CRACK THUD.
The impact caught Morwenna squarely across the ribs. The sound was sickening—the wet crunch of cartilage straining under supernatural force.
HUUUGH!
The air was violently expelled from her lungs in a pained wheeze. The force sent her stumbling backward, three full, unsteady steps that ate up the precious space she needed to reset.
Her shoulder slammed into a broken marble pillar with a bone-jarring THUMP, sending dust and ancient debris cascading around her.
Morwenna lurched forward, coughing violently. A spray of crimson spittle flecked the stone floor.
PHTH!
Her chest burned as if filled with molten lead, every breath a serrated knife in her lungs. But she didn’t retreat.
She didn’t collapse.

She straightened her spine with a guttural growl of defiance, wiping blood from her chin with the back of her gauntlet. In her thirty years of war, she had learned one immutable truth: to stop breathing for even three seconds was to invite the reaper to dinner.
"Cover the left flank!" Valentina’s voice rang out, cutting through the ringing in Morwenna’s ears.

The headmaster’s voice was tight, strained by the sheer magical output required to keep the barrage going, but it possessed an unbreakable steel. "He favors it whenever he pivots away from your blade!"
"He’s compensating for your reach!"
Morwenna didn’t waste breath on a reply. She couldn’t afford to.

Instead, she shifted her stance, her boots scraping against the tile with a decisive SKREEEE. She widened her footing by exactly half a step, closing the tactical gap Valentina had identified with the instinctive precision of a veteran sergeant.
Xerollion attempted to reset. He pivoted away from a probing thrust aimed at his ribs, seeking to reestablish his distance.
But the trap was sprung. The moment his weight shifted, Morwenna was already there, not where he expected her to be, but exactly where the tactical opening existed.
SHHHH TCH!
Her blade flashed in a vicious arc. Xerollion was forced to twist his torso unnaturally far, his spine popping audibly as he contorted to avoid being bisected.
The enchanted steel missed his flesh but tore through his sleeve with the sound of ripping parchment, leaving a long, clean slit across his forearm.
A thin line of fresh blood welled up along the cut, stark against his skin.
"Noted," Xerollion said. His voice was eerily calm, carrying a thread of genuine, almost academic appreciation that felt more threatening than any battle cry. "Remarkable."
"You two communicate with more lethal clarity in the middle of a massacre than most elite units manage on a sunlit parade ground."
His eyes flickered to the blood on his arm. He could feel his Infinite Regeneration already beginning the work, a faint, tingling heat as the cells began to stitch themselves back together.
"We’re not dying," Valentina snapped back.
Her breathing was ragged now, sweat streaming down her temples, causing strands of her silver hair to cling to her flushed skin like spider silk.
Her fingers were twitching, weaving the complex geometric patterns of a new compound spell even as she spoke.
FZZT CRACKLE.
"Not today."
Her eyes locked onto his, burning with a desperate, incandescent fury. "Not to you... Never to you."
The air between them began to hum again, heavier this time, charged with the static of a storm that refused to break.

chapters.title: Chapter 1202. I May Have Underestimated the Desperation of Cornered Prey
paragraphs: Valentina realized that raw power and predictable patterns would only feed his adaptation. She needed to probe the nature of his very existence.
Her fingers began to move in a complex, hypnotic spiral, weaving a rare and dangerous detection casting into the tail end of her next elemental barrage.
This wasn’t just an attack; it was a metaphysical probe designed to strip away illusions, to peel back layers of disguise and reveal the true face of whatever lurked behind his presence.
She had only used this technique twice in her entire career, both times against infiltrators who thought their magic could hide their sins.
VROOOOOM SHHHHIIIINNNN!

A pulse of translucent silver energy rippled outward from her spell, racing toward Xerollion like a wave seeking a shore. Valentina held her breath, waiting for the magical feedback that would signal a successful unraveling.
Instead, there was nothing. The silver wave didn’t crash against a barrier; it simply slid off him, harmlessly deflecting as if he were made of polished diamond.
There was no resistance, no magical recoil, just an eerie, absolute absence of vulnerability. The failure landed in her chest like a cold stone.
"That won’t work either," Xerollion said.
His voice lacked any trace of malice; instead, it held something far more unsettling: patience. He sounded like a professor correcting a promising student who had made a predictable error.
"Whatever lies beneath this mask isn’t hidden by anything a detection spell was ever built to find."
"You’re trying to measure the ocean with a ruler, Valentina."
Valentina’s jaw tightened. Her lips pressed into a thin line, but she said nothing.
She didn’t have the luxury of curiosity. Whatever truth he was withholding would have to wait for a day she survived to ask it.
Her mind filed the revelation away like a bullet in a chamber: ’His true nature is beyond conventional magical comprehension.’
FZZZT BOOM!
She pivoted instantly, refusing to let the moment of doubt linger. She began to weave her spellwork into increasingly chaotic patterns.
Every three to four seconds, she shifted her entire magical methodology.
CRACKLE WHOOSH SHATTER.
Fire became ice; ice became lightning; lightning became raw gravitational force. She never allowed the same elemental combination to repeat twice in succession.

It was a desperate, brilliant strategy designed to sabotage his Full Potential Adaptation to force his mind to constantly restart its analysis, to deny him the data he needed to predict her next move.
It worked. For several agonizing minutes, the adaptation stuttered.

Xerollion’s eyes flickered with micro adjustments as his brain struggled to process the shifting variables. The delay he suffered was measured in precious seconds, but in this dance of death, seconds were the difference between a killing blow and a fatal mistake.
Beneath this magical cacophony, Morwenna remained the silent, deadly constant. She fought with a terrifying economy of motion that made the air itself seem to obey her blade.
SHING. SHING. SHING.
She never wasted a single calorie of energy. Every strike was a calculated expenditure; every retreat was exactly half a step—just enough to avoid a counterattack without conceding ground.
She never overcommitted, never left her flank exposed. She was a surgeon with a sword, operating in the space between his breaths.
SQUELCH.
Twice in quick succession, she found the gaps. A precise slash across his bicep, then a lightning-fast nick across his ribs. Blood painted small, crimson streaks across his clothes.
’God damn it,’ Xerollion thought, his enhanced senses registering the sting.
He watched her move the way she balanced her weight, the way she anticipated the magical backlash from Valentina’s spells to use it as cover.
For a fleeting, dangerous moment, something shifted in his perception. He found himself reassessing the woman he had spent the previous night with.

He had seen the matriarch, the political force, the composed ally. But now, seeing her in the crucible of combat, the true Morwenna surfaced: the ruthless combat instructor who had drilled thousands of soldiers to die without hesitation.
The predator beneath the skin was unmistakable.
CLANG!

Morwenna’s blade met his telekinetic barrier with enough force to send vibrations up his arm. She didn’t recoil; she rolled into the impact, her eyes locked onto his with a cold, unblinking intensity that spoke of a lifetime spent in the slaughter.

For Morwenna, the steel in her hand felt heavier than it ever had before, though not from physical fatigue. The weight was psychological, a crushing pressure that had nothing to do with the blade and everything to do with the man standing across from her.
Every time she caught the specific tilt of that masked head, a micro adjustment of the neck that felt hauntingly familiar, her heart stuttered.

Every time his economy of motion flickered past her at that particular angle, a treacherous part of her mind clawed at the surface, reaching for memories she had spent the entire night trying to bury under layers of duty, grief, and the desperate need to protect her crumbling household.
’No,’ she screamed at herself internally. ’Not now... Not him...’
She shoved the thought down with such violent mental force it felt like a physical blow to her skull. There was no room in this blood-slicked corridor for sentiment.
To entertain that suspicion, even for a heartbeat, felt like a betrayal she wasn’t ready to name aloud—not to Valentina, not to her soldiers, and most terrifyingly, not to herself.
CRACK THOOM!
Valentina felt the shift before she saw it. She felt that specific, cold tightening low in her chest, the intuitive warning that the dance of probing strikes was over.
The time for testing defenses had passed; the time for annihilation had arrived.
"Morwenna, clear the blast radius!" Valentina commanded, her voice dropping an octave into a tone of absolute authority.
Valentina planted her feet wide, her boots grinding into the stone. Both hands rose in intricate, desperate patterns.
FWOOOOOOOSH.

The pages of her grimoire didn’t just flutter; they tore free from their binding entirely, each parchment sheet glowing with an incandescent violet light as they began to orbit her body in a swirling, deadly cyclone.
She was drawing on reserves she normally reserved for collapsing siege towers or ending entire campaigns.
"Forgive me for this," Valentina whispered, though whether she was speaking to her enemies or herself was unclear.
Then, she unleashed it: her strongest working. A catastrophic fusion of ionized lightning and raw gravitational magic.
KRA BOOOOOOOOM!!!
The world disappeared behind a wall of white-hot agony and crushing pressure. The spell didn’t just strike; it detonated.
An expanding ring of violet energy tore outward, the gravitational force shrieking as it twisted the very air.
CRUNCH. SHATTER.
Support columns thirty feet away snapped like dry twigs under the sudden increase in mass. The ceiling above Xerollion gave way instantly, massive slabs of ancient stone plummeting toward him.
THUD THUD CRASH.
The debris created a boiling column of dust and pulverized rock so thick it blotted out what remained of the torchlight.
SHING!
Morwenna didn’t hesitate. She didn’t wait for the dust to settle.
She used the disorientation as her scalpel. Seeing the silhouette of Xerollion struggling beneath the crushing gravity and falling stone, she launched herself forward.
She drove her blade toward a vital point—the exposed throat—with every ounce of her remaining strength.
SQUELCH.
For several agonizing seconds, the combined force of Valentina’s cosmic devastation and Morwenna’s lethal precision actually worked.
The shockwave and the blade’s momentum forced Xerollion backward, his boots skidding across the stone as he was pushed several steps through the chaos.
As the dust began to thin, a figure emerged from the wreckage.

Xerollion stood amidst the rubble, his robes torn to shreds, revealing skin mapped with fresh burns and shallow cuts. He raised a hand to his face, wiping a thin rivulet of blood from the corner of his mouth.
SPLAT.
The blood glistened crimson against his pale skin. When he spoke, his voice carried a new, rougher edge—the sound of a man who was finally beginning to feel the friction of real combat.
"Quite impressive," he said, his breathing measured despite the carnage surrounding him. "Both of you are considerably more dangerous than I anticipated."
"I may have underestimated the desperation of cornered prey."
Valentina didn’t flinch. Sweat cut clean lines through the thick coating of stone dust on her face, her eyes blazing with a terrifying, focused light.
"Save the compliments, you bastard," she snapped, her fingers already twitching in the air as she began weaving the next devastating pattern. "Save them for after we’ve actually finished this."

He raised a hand to his face, wiping a thin rivulet of blood from the corner of his mouth.
SPLAT.
The blood glistened crimson against his pale skin.
When he spoke, his voice carried a new, rougher edge—the sound of a man who was finally beginning to feel the friction of real combat.
"Quite impressive," he said, his breathing measured despite the carnage surrounding him.
"Both of you are considerably more dangerous than I anticipated."
"I may have underestimated the desperation of cornered prey."
Valentina didn’t flinch.
Sweat cut clean lines through the thick coating of stone dust on her face, her eyes blazing with a terrifying, focused light.
"Save the compliments, you bastard," she snapped, her fingers already twitching in the air as she began weaving the next devastating pattern.
"Save them for after we’ve actually finished this."

chapters.title: Chapter 1203. Hope Is Dangerous When Fighting a Predator Who Learns
paragraphs: Valentina meant it, or at least, she screamed it into the void of the corridor until the words became a shield. But beneath the defiance, a cold, honest sliver of her consciousness had already begun to calculate the impossible.

She saw the way his wounds closed; she saw the way his eyes never faltered. Finishing this wasn’t a tactical objective anymore; it was a desperate prayer she had to recite aloud just to keep her muscles from seizing in terror.
But she buried that realization under a mountain of magical fury. A headmaster who allowed the taste of defeat to linger on her tongue mid-battle was already a corpse walking.
FZZZT WHIRRRR!
"Don’t you dare stop!" Valentina roared, her voice cracking with the strain. "Morwenna, now! Push him into the next circle!"
Morwenna heard the raw desperation beneath the command, the way Valentina’s voice wavered like a candle in a hurricane.

She responded not with words, but with a ferocious escalation of violence. She drove in low, her boots skidding across the blood-slicked stone with a SHHHH THUD, her blade becoming a silver blur aimed at his kneecaps.
SHING!

Xerollion was forced into a nightmare of divided focus. He had to split his consciousness between the lethal steel threatening to sever his tendons at his legs and the apocalyptic storm of elemental energy Valentina was conjuring directly above his skull.
CRACKLE BOOM!
Bolts of violet lightning arched around him like angry serpents, forcing him to raise a telekinetic shield that groaned under the pressure.
GRRRR NKKKK.
The sound of his barrier straining against the magical onslaught sounded like grinding tectonic plates.
Then, something miraculous happened: they found the rhythm.

It was a brutal, beautiful synchronization born of necessity. Valentina’s spellwork became the anvil, her devastating castings forcing Xerollion to retreat, to brace, to expend his precious adaptive energy on defense.

Her magic bought Morwenna the precious inches of space needed to close the distance. And in return, Morwenna’s blade became the hammer, her relentless, bone-crushing pressure forcing Xerollion to focus on his immediate survival, which in turn bought Valentina the precious seconds she needed to inhale, to steady her hands, and to weave the next impossible spell.
THUD. SLICE. CRACK.
To the soldiers watching from the safety of the far archway, the scene was terrifying. They saw their leaders, the untouchable Headmaster and the legendary Commander, dismantling a godlike entity.
For the first time since the slaughter began, the air didn’t smell just of death; it smelled of hope.
"Hold the line!" one soldier whispered hoarsely, his knuckles white around his spear. "Look at them... they’re actually doing it!"
Valentina seized the moment.
"This is for everyone you’ve taken!" she screamed, her eyes glowing with pure arcane light.
Instead of a bolt, she channeled a compressed wind, casting a vacuum sphere designed to collapse inward with the force of a collapsing star.
WHOOOOOO SHHHH!
The spell struck Xerollion’s left flank like a physical fist. The air was violently ripped from around his lungs, leaving him gasping in a momentary void of oxygen.
HUUUGH!
His ribs creaked under the sudden pressure differential, and his head snapped sideways as the vacuum staggered him half a step.
"Now, Morwenna! END IT!" Valentina’s voice was almost gone, spent from the exertion.
Morwenna didn’t hesitate. She was already mid-leap, her body coiled like a spring unleashed.
She drove her blade in at a vicious, diagonal angle, a strike designed to bypass his guard and sever his carotid artery in one clean motion. It was the perfect killing blow.
SHHHH TCH!
The blade whistled through the air, mere millimeters from his exposed throat. But the air suddenly froze.
CLANG.
In a display of speed that defied human comprehension, Xerollion’s hand shot up. His fingers clamped around Morwenna’s wrist like a vice made of enchanted steel.
CRUNCH.

The sound of her bones grinding against the pressure of his grip echoed in the sudden silence. The blade stopped dead, the razor-sharp tip trembling violently in the microscopic gap between the steel and his jugular.
Both women froze. Morwenna’s breath came in ragged, burning gasps, her sweat dripping onto the blade.

Xerollion’s masked face was inches from hers, his breath cold against her cheek. The tension in the corridor was so thick it felt as though the next heartbeat would shatter the very foundations of the castle.
Time seemed to solidify into something physical, a suspended amber moment where nothing existed but the friction between Morwenna’s blade and Xerollion’s pulse.
Morwenna’s entire body was coiled, every muscle fiber screaming as she threw her weight forward, trying to force those final, fatal millimeters.
Her arm shook violently, not from weakness, but from the sheer impossibility of moving an immovable object.
GRRRRR...
The sound came from Morwenna’s own teeth gritted in agony. Xerollion’s grip was absolute.
His fingers didn’t just hold her wrist; they seemed to fuse with it, his supernatural strength threatening to splinter her radius and ulna like dry kindling.
CRACKLE.
The tendons in her forearm strained to the point of tearing.

Yet, beneath the violence of the hold, something deeply unsettling stirred in Morwenna’s mind. In that terrifying stillness, she looked into the hollow darkness of his mask and saw something that wasn’t rage.
It was... consideration. As if he weren’t resisting her attack but weighing it as if a part of him were genuinely contemplating whether to simply step aside and let her finish what she started.
’Is he... hesitating?’ The thought flashed through her mind like lightning. ’Is he letting me win?’
ZAP BOOOOOM!!!

The question was answered by a scream of displaced air. Valentina, seeing the opening created by the locked blades, didn’t hesitate. She channeled every remaining spark of her willpower into a narrow, hyper-focused spear of concentrated lightning.
SHHHHHHH THWACK!
The bolt streaked across the corridor like a lance of pure white wrath, aimed precisely at the exposed gap in Xerollion’s ribs.

He couldn’t block it without exposing his throat to Morwenna, and he couldn’t stay still without being incinerated. With a fluid, almost disdainful twist of his torso, he released Morwenna’s wrist and spun away.
WHOOSH.
Morwenna stumbled backward from the sudden loss of resistance, her boots skidding on blood and stone. She caught herself against a crumbling wall, her chest heaving in ragged, desperate gulps.
For one heartbeat, across the smoking wreckage of the corridor, she and Valentina locked eyes. In that shared glance, there was something fragile and terrifying: hope.
But hope is a dangerous thing when fighting a predator who learns.
VROOOOOOM.

The air began to hum again, but this time the sound was different—deeper, more predatory. Xerollion wasn’t reacting anymore; he was anticipating. His foresight and divine perception had fused into a singular, flawless engine of calculation.

He was no longer fighting two women; he was solving a puzzle. He watched the micro fluctuations in Valentina’s mana reserves; he measured the precise millisecond Morwenna’s footing faltered after her last lunge.
Then, he found it.
The seam.
The microscopic flaw in their perfect synchronization.
It was a moment that lasted less than a heartbeat. Valentina’s lungs burned as she drew a ragged breath, her grimoire’s pages fluttering down to rest like dead leaves around her.
Morwenna, still reeling from the bone-deep ache in her wrist, was caught half a step off balance, her center of gravity betrayed by her own momentum.
To a mortal, it was a blink.
To Xerollion, it was an eternity.
WHAM!
Before Morwenna could even register his movement, he was inside her guard. His hand shot out like a striking viper, seizing her wrist again, but this time there was no hesitation.
He twisted, using her own momentum against her, and slammed her bodily into the stone floor.
CRUNCH.
The impact was brutal. Morwenna’s back hit the masonry with a sound like breaking timber. The air fled her lungs in a pained "GAK" as her vision swam with black spots.
Her consciousness flickered like a dying flame, the world tilting into darkness.
But he didn’t stop. He couldn’t.
Xerollion pivoted on his heel with terrifying grace, his boots kicking up sparks from the stone. He moved toward Valentina before her next spell could even form in her mind.
His hand shot forward, fingers closing around her throat with the inevitability of a closing trap.
THUD.
He lifted her off the ground. Valentina’s boots dangled uselessly inches above the blood-stained tiles.
Her hands clawed weakly at his forearm, her face flushing a dangerous crimson as her airway collapsed.
GASP... HHHH...
"You’ve held back long enough, Valentina," Xerollion said.
His voice was terrifyingly calm, devoid of any heat, echoing off the ruined walls. Behind the mask, his eyes burned with a cold, ancient light as he stared down at the weakening woman in his grasp.
"It’s time you learned what happens when my patience finally runs out."

chapters.title: Chapter 1204. How Long Can You Maintain the Illusion Before the Mask Cracks?
paragraphs: Behind him, sprawled across the cracked and blood-slicked masonry, Morwenna stirred. Her world was a spinning kaleidoscope of agony and ringing silence.
BEEEEEEEEEEEE...!
The high-pitched whine in her ears drowned out everything else as she forced one eye open, each movement feeling like hot glass sliding through her veins.
Through the haze of pain and the copper tang of blood filling her mouth, she saw him. She saw the silhouette of the man who held Valentina aloft like a broken doll.
A sound tore itself from her throat—not a battle cry, not a scream, but something far worse: a raw, wordless sound of pure, unadulterated grief.
It was a protest aimed at the universe, at the cruelty of fate, and at the man she had shared the intimacy of skin and breath with only days earlier.
’How?’ The question screamed in the silence of her mind. ’How could you be this monster?’
’How could you be him?’
Every instinct she had forged through thirty years of brutal warfare screamed at her to rise, to draw steel, to die on her feet. But her body was a traitor.
Her skull throbbed with a dull, distant agony where it had met the stone, and her limbs felt like they had been replaced with lead. She could not move fast enough to matter.
She could only lie there, a helpless spectator to a slaughter, watching the man she thought she knew become the architect of her destruction.
GASP... HHHH... CRACKLE.
Valentina’s struggle was growing weaker. Her face, once flushed with the fire of spellcasting, was now fading to a sickly, pale lavender.

Her fingers clawed uselessly at Xerollion’s forearm, her nails leaving faint red crescents in his skin that healed almost instantly. Her grimoire lay several feet away, dark, silent, and tantalizingly out of reach—a tombstone for her power.
The realization settled over Valentina with a terrifying, detached clarity: ’This is how it ends.’
Her vision began to tunnel, the edges of the world fraying into blackness.
Xerollion’s free hand began to glow.
VROOOOOOOOM.

A sphere of violet black energy, dense as a dying star and crackling with malevolent intent, began to coil in his palm. The air around his hand warped and screamed as the magical pressure intensified.
He was preparing to deliver the coup de grace, a spell designed to erase whatever remained of Valentina’s consciousness.
"Die with the dignity you fought so hard to maintain," Xerollion murmured, his voice like grinding stone.
WHAM!!!
Just as the energy reached its crescendo, a blur of motion erupted from the periphery. It wasn’t a spell; it was pure, kinetic fury.
SHHHH THWACK!
A strike, impossibly fast and carrying the force of a battering ram, slammed into Xerollion’s extended arm. The impact was so violent that the bone in his forearm audibly groaned under the stress.
CRUNCH.
The magical sphere detonated prematurely in a harmless shower of sparks, and the sudden shock forced his fingers to spasm open.
Valentina dropped like a stone.
THUD.
She collapsed onto her hands and knees, retching and gasping, her lungs burning as she drank in air in desperate, convulsing gulps.
COUGH. WHEEZE.
Her vision swam as she looked up through tear-blurred eyes.
The attacker didn’t retreat. The figure stepped forward with deliberate, measured steps, moving directly into the kill zone.
The stranger planted their feet between the gasping headmaster and the towering threat, shoulders squared, hands ready, radiating an aura of unmistakable, unshakable protective intent.
The dust settled around the newcomer’s boots. The light from the dying torches caught the glint of armor and the steady rise and fall of a chest that knew no fear.
Rex Rexilion had arrived.
"That’s enough."
The words didn’t carry the desperate scream of a survivor or the frantic command of a soldier. They were measured.
They were heavy. They possessed the kind of absolute certainty that could cut through the chaos of a collapsing corridor like a blade through silk.
Rex Rexilion stood there, his silhouette framed by the flickering torchlight and the swirling dust of the magical devastation.
His face was a mask of carefully constructed courage, a perfect, almost theatrical blend of righteous anger and unshakable resolve.
To any observer, he was the archetype made flesh: the hero who had finally decided to stop watching from the sidelines and claim his destiny.
"I won’t let you hurt them any further," Rex declared, his voice carrying across the stone chamber with the authority of a king.
His hands clenched into fists at his sides, the muscles in his forearms cording like steel cables.
A stunned, deathly silence descended upon the remaining soldiers.
"Is that... Rex?" one whispered, the words barely audible over the crackle of residual lightning. "He’s actually... he’s standing up to him."
A wave of astonishment rolled through the ranks; they watched with bated breath as the man they had known as a stalwart companion finally stepped into the light as their protector.
Across the carnage, Xerollion did not attack. He did not snarl.
Instead, he simply stood there, his masked head tilting to the side with a slow, predatory curiosity.
’Another plan... huh... it seems like I had to play the drama like the usual.’

Behind that impassive mask, Xerollion’s mind was racing at speeds no mortal could comprehend. His Divine Perception wasn’t just seeing Rex; it was dissecting him. He felt something distinctly... wrong.

A signature of energy was bleeding off the newcomer, a resonant frequency that felt disturbingly familiar. It was like hearing a melody played on two different instruments: one perfect, one slightly off-key.
The energy reading carried an almost identical quality to his own power, but it fell just short of perfection. It was a mirror that had been slightly warped.
"What are you?" Xerollion wondered, his interest piqued far more than his anger. "A shadow? A construct? A memory given flesh?"
The tension between them became a physical thing, a live wire stretched to the breaking point. The air between them hummed with the latent energy of two apex predators recognizing one another.
Xerollion took a single step forward, the sound of his boot grinding against broken stone echoing like a gunshot.
CRUNCH.
He lowered his voice, dropping it to a conspiratorial whisper that seemed to slice through the ambient noise of Valentina’s labored breathing and Morwenna’s pained whimpering.
"Interesting," Xerollion said softly, the word dripping with a cold, analytical amusement. "Standing here to protect them, Rex Rexilion."
"Playing the part of the stalwart guardian... The noble savior."
He paused, his masked gaze boring into Rex’s eyes as if trying to peel back the skin and read the soul beneath.
"I’m curious," Xerollion continued, his voice growing colder, more dangerous. "I’m curious exactly how far you’re willing to carry this role you’ve been playing."
"How long can you maintain the illusion before the mask cracks and shows me what’s truly underneath?"

The tension between them became a physical thing, a live wire stretched to the breaking point.
The air between them hummed with the latent energy of two apex predators recognizing one another.
Xerollion took a single step forward, the sound of his boot grinding against broken stone echoing like a gunshot.
CRUNCH.
He lowered his voice, dropping it to a conspiratorial whisper that seemed to slice through the ambient noise of Valentina’s labored breathing and Morwenna’s pained whimpering.
"Interesting," Xerollion said softly, the word dripping with a cold, analytical amusement.
"Standing here to protect them, Rex Rexilion."
"Playing the part of the stalwart guardian...
The noble savior."
He paused, his masked gaze boring into Rex’s eyes as if trying to peel back the skin and read the soul beneath.
"I’m curious," Xerollion continued, his voice growing colder, more dangerous.
"I’m curious exactly how far you’re willing to carry this role you’ve been playing."
"How long can you maintain the illusion before the mask cracks and shows me what’s truly underneath?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1205. A Masterpiece Painted by Someone Who Had Seen the Subject Once
paragraphs: The ruined corridor became a stage of impossible stillness. In the center of the carnage, Valentina and Morwenna lay like broken offerings, one gasping for air, the other drowning in pain, while between them stood two titans.
On one side, Rex Rexilion: the picture of heroic defiance, his stance unshakable, his eyes blazing with a righteous fire that seemed to warm even the cold stone.
On the other, Xerollion: a predator wrapped in shadow, his masked face unreadable, studying his opponent with the detached fascination of a scientist examining a new species of insect.
Every remaining soldier held their breath. The silence was absolute, broken only by the distant drip of blood from a cracked ceiling and the ragged, wet coughs of the wounded.
No one could have predicted this standoff. No one could have guessed that this wasn’t a battle between hero and villain but a confrontation between truth and its echo.
Because only one of them knew: the man standing across from him was not a man at all. He was a mirror.
A shadow.
A flawless, incomplete imitation.
THUM THUM. THUM THUM.
The heartbeat of the room seemed to accelerate as the tension reached its breaking point. Then, the silence didn’t just break; it shattered.
SHHHH WHAM!
Rex Rexilion moved. He didn’t just lunge; he exploded forward with a burst of kinetic energy that tore up the stone beneath his boots.
CRACK.

The attack was terrifyingly familiar to anyone who had ever trained alongside the real Rex. It was a flawless execution of the Dragon Strike lunge, a technique that required perfect synchronization between physical momentum and telekinetic acceleration.
WHOOSH BOOM!

As Rex swung his fist, a ripple of invisible force preceded the strike, amplifying the impact tenfold. It was the exact signature of Rex’s fighting style: the precise marriage of martial arts mastery and telekinetic enhancement.
To the watching soldiers, it was a spectacle of divine heroism.
To Xerollion, it was a grotesque parody.
CLANG!
Xerollion didn’t even flinch. With a movement that was almost insulting in its economy, he raised his forearm to meet the blow.
The impact sent a shockwave through the corridor, cracking the floor tiles beneath them, but Xerollion remained unmoved.
VROOOOOM.
The telekinetic energy dissipated against his own superior barrier like water against a cliff face.
Rex didn’t relent. He spun on his heel, the motion fluid and deadly, launching a follow-up kick aimed at Xerollion’s temple while simultaneously manifesting a telekinetic blade to slice at his ribs.
SWISH SHING!
The choreography was perfect, a seamless transition from close-quarters combat to mid-range magical assault.
Xerollion parried each strike with terrifying ease. He moved with a lazy, almost bored grace, deflecting the strikes not with desperation, but with the casual flick of a wrist.
Yet, his body language betrayed him; there was a visible spark of something resembling pleasure in his movements. He was relishing this. He was watching himself fight through another’s eyes.
THUD. CRACK. WHACK.

The sounds of their clashing power echoed like thunderclaps in the confined space. Rex’s strikes were relentless, each one carrying the full weight of a man who believed he was fighting for salvation.
He threw a devastating left hook, reinforced by a burst of psychic pressure that made the very air scream.
KRA KOOOOM!
Xerollion caught the fist. His fingers wrapped around Rex’s knuckles with a sound of grinding bone.
GRRRRK.
The pressure was immense, but Xerollion didn’t push back with anger; he pushed back with curiosity.
As he deflected the next punch, a lightning-fast jab that would have shattered a normal man’s ribs, Xerollion leaned in close, his breath ghosting past Rex’s ear.
His voice was a low, melodic murmur that cut through the ringing violence of the fight.
"Ninety seven point three," Xerollion whispered, the numbers dripping with cold, mathematical cruelty.
He twisted Rex’s wrist aside with a contemptuous flick, sending the ’hero’ stumbling back. "A remarkable performance. Truly."
A dark chuckle rumbled behind his mask as he resettled into his combat stance, his eyes glowing brighter as he prepared to dismantle the illusion.
"I wonder," Xerollion mused, his voice carrying a razor-sharp edge of mockery, "exactly which part of me you couldn’t quite copy."

Rex Rexilion offered no verbal reply. Words were for men; this was a collision of forces. He simply roared a sound that was more of a psychic shockwave than a human vocalization and plunged back into the fray.
BOOOOOM!
The corridor became a vortex of violence. The exchange that followed transcended ordinary combat; it became a spectacle of impossible physics.
Rex launched into a devastating sequence: a spinning crescent kick that tore through the air with a WHOOSH, immediately followed by a telekinetic thrust that aimed to puncture Xerollion’s sternum.
SHHH THWACK!
Xerollion countered with a reverse palm strike that met the kick midair, the impact creating a concussive blast that sent debris spiraling outward like shrapnel.
CLANG! CRASH!
The surrounding battlefield fell into a deathly, hypnotic hush. The war itself seemed to pause.
Soldiers from Aethelgard and the ruthless Underlayer alike lowered their weapons. Blood-soaked blades dripped uselessly to the floor as eyes fixed in terrified fascination on the center of the storm.
It was as if the universe itself had drawn a breath and held it, unwilling to miss a single second of this grotesque mirror match.
They weren’t watching two men fight; they were watching a man fight his own reflection, each strike a perfect, devastating echo of the other.
CRACK THUD!

Rex landed a series of rapid-fire punches, each one reinforced by compressed air. Xerollion parried them with surgical precision, his movements so identical to Rex’s that it created an optical illusion, a blurring of two bodies becoming one.
WHACK. WHACK. WHACK.
The sound was rhythmic, almost musical, punctuated by the wet SPLAT of blood spattering from where Rex’s knuckles grazed Xerollion’s cheek.
In the Underlayer ranks, Cassandra and Gorvasha stood frozen. A profound, unsettling confusion overrode their usual predatory instincts.
"How?" Gorvasha hissed, his voice cracking with disbelief. "How can anyone mimic his rhythm so perfectly?!"
"Not even his own students can anticipate his feints like that."
Cassandra didn’t answer. Her eyes were narrowed, tracking the impossible choreography.
"It’s not mimicry," she whispered, a chill running down her spine. "It’s... recognition."

On the opposite side, among the battered remnants of Aethelgard, hope was a wildfire spreading through the despair. The soldiers, bruised and broken, saw in Rex Rexilion the miracle they had been praying for.
"It has to be him," a young soldier sobbed, her voice breaking as fresh tears carved clean tracks through the grime and dried blood on her cheeks. "Look at him!"
"Look at how he moves! Nobody else could fight like that."
"Nobody else has that soul in their strikes!" Her companion nodded fervently, gripping a broken spear as if Rex’s sheer presence could heal their wounds.
Yet, amidst the rising tide of hope, one pair of eyes saw the cracks in the foundation.

Valentina, slumped against a crumbling wall, her lungs still burning from the near asphyxiation, watched through a haze of pain. Her scholarly mind, trained to detect the slightest anomaly in magical theory, couldn’t help but catalog the details.
She watched the way Rex’s weight shifted during a pivot; it was correct, but the timing was... mechanical.
His movements were a fraction of a second too precise.
Too rehearsed.
’There,’ she thought, her heart beginning to sink as a cold dread replaced the heat of her exhaustion. ’His shoulders.’
In every training yard she had ever observed, Rex’s movements possessed a certain fluid warmth, a spontaneous grace born of human instinct.
But this Rex... this Rex moved with a terrifying, rigid perfection.

There was a stiffness in his shoulders, a lack of the micro adjustments that come from living flesh and blood. He was moving like a masterpiece painted by someone who had seen the subject once but never touched it.
KRA KOOOM!
Another clash of telekinetic force shook the foundations of the corridor, sending a cloud of choking dust between the two fighters.
As the smoke cleared, the two figures emerged again, poised and deadly, the illusion of heroism continuing to dazzle the masses even as the truth began to whisper to those who knew how to listen.

chapters.title: Chapter 1206. There’s a Difference Between Knowing How to Move and Knowing Why
paragraphs: The violence escalated from a clash of steel and muscle to something far more fundamental: a war of reality itself.
Rex Rexilion’s next move was a cataclysm. His hands blurred as he wove together two of the most devastating disciplines in existence.
VROOOOOOM CRACKLE!
With his left hand, he summoned the fury of Elemental Mastery, conjuring a torrent of superheated plasma that screamed through the air like a dragon’s breath.
Simultaneously, his right hand twisted in a complex gesture of Gravity Manipulationgravity manipulation.
The air around the plasma stream didn’t just burn; it collapsed inward, creating a localized gravitational well that dragged the flames into a spinning, hyperdense vortex.
WHOOOOOOOM!
The attack roared toward Xerollion, a spiraling lance of elemental destruction and crushing force. But Xerollion did not flinch.
He didn’t even adopt a defensive stance. Instead, he met the vortex head-on with the terrifying nonchalance of a god meeting a child’s tantrum.

Because he was not merely fighting an opponent; he was fighting a mirror image of his own genius. Every technique Rex unleashed was a technique Xerollion had perfected, refined, and understood down to its atomic structure.
He knew the precise harmonic frequency at which the plasma would destabilize. He knew exactly how much gravitational pressure would cause the construct’s telekinetic shield to buckle.
SHHHHH BOOM!
Xerollion raised a single finger. A microburst of countergravitational energy met the vortex, canceling out the momentum in a spectacular explosion of displaced air and sparks.
KRA KOOOOM!
The shockwave sent dust and blood-stained debris cascading across the corridor floor like shrapnel.

For several minutes, the corridor became a kaleidoscope of impossible phenomena: elemental bursts of crimson and azure collided in midair, canceling each other out in blinding flashes of white light, while overlapping gravitational fields twisted the very light around them, making the two fighters appear to warp and stretch like phantoms.
To the soldiers watching, paralyzed by awe, it looked like an impossible stalemate between two gods locked in an eternal dance of destruction.
But the illusion of balance was rotting from within.
WHACK. CRUNCH. THUD.
Xerollion began to close the distance. His movements became sharper and more economical, each parry more devastating than the last.
He wasn’t just deflecting Rex’s attacks anymore; he was redirecting them back at the construct with lethal intent.
"You know the biggest problem with fighting your own reflection?" Xerollion’s voice rang out through the thunder of clashing magic, cold and utterly amused.
He caught Rex’s wrist mid-swing GRIP and twisted, sending a jolt of pain through the construct’s simulated nervous system. "I already know exactly what you’re going to do next."
He stepped inside Rex’s guard, his elbow connecting with the construct’s jaw with a wet, bone-deep CRACK.
"Because I thought of it," Xerollion whispered, his eyes burning behind the mask, "before you were ever created."
The tide turned with brutal efficiency. Xerollion stopped playing.

The curiosity faded, replaced by the cold satisfaction of a predator dismantling a trap. Every attack Rex unleashed was met with a counter that exploited a microscopic flaw in the construct’s programming.
When Rex attempted a telekinetic shield, Xerollion struck the exact pressure point where the energy was most vulnerable, shattering it like glass.
SHATTER CRACK!
THUD!
A devastating roundhouse kick caught Rex square in the ribs.

Even though Rex was an energy-based construct, the magical feedback was so precise that his form began to manifest physical damage; the simulated bones splintered, and a spray of synthetic, blood-red energy spattered across the stone floor.
SPLAT.
CRUNCH.

Xerollion followed up with a brutal uppercut that lifted the ’hero’ off his feet, sending him staggering backward. Rex’s breathing, the simulated, labored gasping of a human, became more ragged, more desperate.
Blood or whatever crimson essence the construct bled streaked across Rex’s face, painting the picture of a dying hero.
The soldiers’ hope began to waver as they saw their savior falter, bleeding and broken under the relentless onslaught of the monster who seemed to know his every heartbeat before he even felt it.
The violence took on a grotesque, uncanny quality. As Xerollion dismantled the construct, the damage appeared not as random trauma but as a deliberate anatomical dissection.

Bruises bloomed across Rex’s skin deep, violet contusions that shouldn’t have been possible on something made of light and data and blood welled from lacerations that followed the exact surgical lines of human vulnerability.
Every cut was a statement: ’I know where you are fragile.’
CRACK THUD.
Xerollion drove a fist into a specific point along Rex’s ribcage. It wasn’t a random strike; it was the exact nexus where the construct’s magical circulatory system maintained its equilibrium.
SPLAT.
A spray of crimson essence erupted from Rex’s mouth as his ribs simulated but terrifyingly convincing buckled inward with a wet, grinding sound.
Rex staggered backward, his knees buckling, his simulated breathing coming in ragged, wet gasps that made the horrified soldiers flinch.
Yet, the construct did not falter. It could not falter.

Rex Rexilion threw himself back into the fray with a relentless, mechanical fury. For several agonizing minutes, the fight descended into something almost hauntingly beautiful, a macabre ballet of perfect symmetry.
Two identical figures moved through techniques so intertwined that watching them felt like witnessing a man engaged in a schizophrenic argument with his own shadow.
WHOOSH SHINK!
A spinning crescent kick, a move Xerollion himself had once used to shatter Kaeleth’s fragments, tore through the air. Instantly, the construct mirrored it with an identical counter.

Both fighters adjusted mid-motion with the same instinctive correction, the same subtle shift of weight on the balls of their feet, and the same microscopic pause before committing to the strike. It was the ghost of Rex’s muscle memory manifesting in a puppet.
Xerollion caught a lightning-fast jab on his forearm.
THUD.
The shockwave traveled up his arm, vibrating through his bones. A thin smile touched the corners of his mouth beneath the mask.
"You fight well," Xerollion admitted, his voice carrying over the crackle of residual magic, "for something built from behavior data rather than lived experience."
His grip tightened on Rex’s wrist as they locked together, foreheads nearly touching. "But there’s a difference between knowing how to move and knowing why you move."
"And that difference... that’s where you die."
Inside the construct’s core, a silent, cold intelligence flickered a cascade of data processing at impossible speeds.
[SYSTEM ALERT: Energy signature analysis complete.]
[Construct confirmed.]
[Behavioral fidelity: 97.3%.]
[Combat dataset current as of last synchronization.]
[WARNING: Structural integrity compromised.]
[Deviation increasing under sustained load.]
[Neural magical pathways destabilizing.]
Rex Rexilion could not process fear, but his programming demanded escalation. He answered Xerollion’s taunt with the only language he possessed: violence.
VROOOOOM!

Rex lunged forward, driving a palm strike aimed directly at Xerollion’s sternum. The strike was wrapped in a razor-thin shell of condensed telekinetic force, vibrating at a frequency designed to shatter magical barriers.
It was the exact technique Rex had deployed weeks earlier against Kaeleth’s fragments—the same lethal precision, the same devastating follow-through.
Xerollion didn’t dodge. He met it.
BOOOOOOOOOM!!!
Xerollion met the palm with his own, palm to palm. The collision was catastrophic.
A perfect circle of compressed air exploded outward from the point of contact, forming a visible ring of pressure that tore through the remaining air in the corridor.
CRACKLE CRUNCH.

The floor beneath them couldn’t withstand the simultaneous release of opposing gravitational and telekinetic energies; the ancient stone shattered in a spreading web of fractures that spiderwebbed outward from their feet, sending chunks of masonry flying like shrapnel.
For a heartbeat, they remained locked in that impossible embrace, two mirrors facing each other, one cracking under the pressure of reality while the other remained unyielding as stone.

"You fight well," Xerollion admitted, his voice carrying over the crackle of residual magic, "for something built from behavior data rather than lived experience."
His grip tightened on Rex’s wrist as they locked together, foreheads nearly touching.
"But there’s a difference between knowing how to move and knowing why you move."
"And that difference... that’s where you die."
Inside the construct’s core, a silent, cold intelligence flickered a cascade of data processing at impossible speeds.
[SYSTEM ALERT: Energy signature analysis complete.]
[Construct confirmed.]
[Behavioral fidelity: 97.3%.]
[Combat dataset current as of last synchronization.]
[WARNING: Structural integrity compromised.]
[Deviation increasing under sustained load.]
[Neural magical pathways destabilizing.]
Rex Rexilion could not process fear, but his programming demanded escalation.
He answered Xerollion’s taunt with the only language he possessed: violence.
VROOOOOM!
Rex lunged forward, driving a palm strike aimed directly at Xerollion’s sternum.
The strike was wrapped in a razor-thin shell of condensed telekinetic force, vibrating at a frequency designed to shatter magical barriers.
It was the exact technique Rex had deployed weeks earlier against Kaeleth’s fragments—the same lethal precision, the same devastating follow-through.
Xerollion didn’t dodge.
He met it.
BOOOOOOOOOM!!!
Xerollion met the palm with his own, palm to palm.
The collision was catastrophic.
A perfect circle of compressed air exploded outward from the point of contact, forming a visible ring of pressure that tore through the remaining air in the corridor.
CRACKLE CRUNCH.

The floor beneath them couldn’t withstand the simultaneous release of opposing gravitational and telekinetic energies; the ancient stone shattered in a spreading web of fractures that spiderwebbed outward from their feet, sending chunks of masonry flying like shrapnel.
For a heartbeat, they remained locked in that impossible embrace, two mirrors facing each other, one cracking under the pressure of reality while the other remained unyielding as stone.

chapters.title: Chapter 1207. You’re Starting to Think for Yourself, Aren’t You, Little Echo?
paragraphs: "That one almost had something new in it."
Xerollion didn’t pull away.
Instead, he maintained the palm-to-palm lock, the grinding pressure between their hands creating a high-pitched whine of displaced air.
He leaned forward, his masked face inches from the construct’s, studying the way the simulated light flickered in Rex’s pupils.
"Tell me, little echo," Xerollion purred, his voice dripping with a sadistic fascination. "Did you improvise that variation on your own?"
"Or is that still something I taught you how to do before you were even conceived?"
For a heartbeat that felt like an eternity, something impossible happened. The construct’s expression didn’t just shift; it fractured.
The heroic mask slipped, revealing something raw, something dark, and something unmistakably frustrated.
It wasn’t a programmed response; it was a flicker of genuine, impotent rage that burned through the data.
SHHH THWIP!
The construct broke the lock with a violent, unnatural twist of its wrist, the motion so sudden it sounded like a whip cracking. Before Xerollion could reset, Rex launched into a vicious low sweep.
WHOOSH!
The leg swept across the stone, sending sparks flying where it grazed the floor. When Xerollion hopped back to avoid the sweep, the construct didn’t pause; it flowed.
KRA KOOOOM!
Rex exploded upward. His fist came screaming from the ground in a devastating uppercut, but this wasn’t just muscle.

At the moment of impact, he triggered a micro burst of Gravity Manipulationgravity manipulation. The gravitational field around his fist didn’t just push; it imploded, doubling the kinetic energy in a fraction of a second.
The air itself seemed to shatter around the punch.
Xerollion didn’t dodge. He didn’t parry.
He simply... let it happen.
CRACK THUD!!!
The sound was sickening. It was the sound of a sledgehammer hitting a concrete pillar.
Xerollion’s head snapped sideways with such violent force that his vertebrae audibly shifted CLACK and he was launched backward.

His boots skidded across the debris-strewn floor, carving two deep trenches in the stone as he fought to maintain balance. A thin, crimson line of blood split the corner of his mouth, stark against his pale skin.
"NO!" a soldier from Aethelgard screamed, a sound of pure, desperate hope. "He hit him! He actually hit him!"
The corridor erupted in a wave of audible gasps. For one electric, terrifying moment, the entire war stopped.
The soldiers, the Underlayer rebels, and the wounded—they all saw it. They saw the monster bleeding.
They saw the hero winning. The tide hadn’t just turned; it felt as though it had been torn away by force.
Xerollion came to a halt, his chest rising and falling in slow, measured breaths. He reached up with two fingers and wiped the blood from his lip.
Then, he did something that sent a new chill through the onlookers: he smiled.
"There it is."
Xerollion worked his jaw experimentally. With a wet, grinding sound, CRUNCH, CRUNCH, CRUNCH the bone snapped back into its perfect alignment.
His voice came out not angry but almost delighted, like a child who had just seen a new trick from a favorite toy.

"I wanted to see how hard you’d commit once you thought you had an opening," Xerollion said, stepping forward again, his aura beginning to darken, the shadows around his feet twisting like living things. "I needed to see if you possessed the desperation of a living creature when the prey thinks it has won."
His eyes burned through the mask with a newfound hunger.
"Good... That’s excellent data."
"Now I know exactly how much pressure it takes to make you try."
The construct could not comprehend irony. It could not understand that its greatest triumph, the blood on Xerollion’s lip, was nothing more than a data point in a controlled experiment.
To the construct, the staggered monster was a weakness to be exploited.
VROOOOOM WHACK!
Rex lunged. He closed the distance with terrifying speed, launching a relentless barrage of strikes designed to overwhelm.
THUD. CRUNCH. WHACK.

Xerollion deliberately lowered his guard, allowing the construct to land two devastating blows. A fist sank into his ribs with the sound of grinding stone, GRIND CRACK, followed by a spinning kick that connected squarely with his shoulder with a bone-jarring THWACK.
But there was no recoil.
No pain.
No stumble.
The wounds closed instantly, the flesh knitting back together with an obscene, supernatural speed that made the violence feel hollow.
Xerollion didn’t just absorb the blows; he fed on them.
Each impact was a tactile lesson: ’How much force? How fast? What is the exact decay rate of the energy behind the strike?’
"Impressive," Xerollion muttered through the blood that still stained his teeth. "Your aggression spikes when you perceive vulnerability... Fascinating."
From her position against the crumbling wall, Valentina watched, her breath shallow and ragged. The hope that had briefly ignited in the Aethelgard ranks was flickering like a candle in a hurricane.
Her eyes, sharp with decades of academic and tactical observation, refused to blink. She wasn’t looking at the spectacle; she was looking at the rhythm.
’Something is wrong,’ she thought, a cold, poisonous seed of doubt taking root in her gut. ’The cadence... it’s too perfect. Too rehearsed.’
She had spent years watching students spar, watching them hesitate, watching them flinch, and watching them make mistakes born of fear or exhaustion.
But this? This was a performance.
The way Rex’s attacks landed felt less like a desperate struggle for survival and more like a series of predetermined outcomes being executed with flawless timing.

She filed it away in the vault of her mind, the same vault that had saved her through countless political assassinations and magical coups. She said nothing, but her hand trembled as she gripped her robes.
KRA KOOOOM!
The fight spiraled into a frenzy of escalating devastation. The two identical figures became blurs of motion across the wreckage of the corridor.
SHHHHH BOOM!

Elemental bursts of searing flame and freezing ice collided, scorching fresh black scars into the already charred stone. Gravitational distortions tore loose massive chunks of the ceiling, which fell like meteors around the combatants.
CRASH! THUD!
Neither fighter acknowledged the debris; they were locked in a private hell of their own making.
Then, the construct unleashed something that made the Underlayer soldiers freeze in genuine terror.
WHIRRRRR CRACKLE BOOM!
Rex didn’t just use fire or wind; he fused them. He drew both hands together, spinning them in a complex, overlapping pattern that tore the very air apart.
A compressed storm of hurricane-force wind and jagged lightning began to spiral upward, layering itself into a single, screaming column of elemental annihilation.

It was a technique that shouldn’t exist: a spontaneous synthesis created by the construct extrapolating fragments of Rex’s own repertoire, weaving them into a lethal new hybrid without ever being taught the formula.
The column of storm roared toward Xerollion, lightning arcing off the stone floor and sending sparks dancing across the debris.
ZZZZZT KRAK!
Xerollion didn’t retreat. He didn’t brace.
He simply stood there, his cloak billowing in the unnatural wind, his eyes locked on the swirling vortex of death approaching him.
For the first time since the battle began, the predatory amusement died down. In its place came something else: something almost resembling genuine, childlike curiosity.
"Oh?" Xerollion whispered, his voice barely audible beneath the howling storm. "So you’ve learned to synthesize."
"You’re starting to think for yourself, aren’t you, little echo?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1208. Let’s See How Long You Can Hold Onto Your Desperation
paragraphs: "Improvisation."
Xerollion murmured the word like a prayer to a dark god. The storm column roared toward him, a shrieking pillar of lightning and hurricane force that threatened to strip the flesh from his bones.
ZZZZZT KRAAAAA BOOM!
But Xerollion did not flinch. Instead, he raised a single hand, fingers splayed as if plucking invisible strings.
SHHHHH VROOOOM!
From his palm erupted a burst of raw, unfiltered elemental force, but it wasn’t just power. It was power threaded with harmonic frequencies that defied logic.

This was a frequency the construct had no record of, no resonance profile in its vast database, because it was a technique Rex himself had only finished refining in the weeks after the construct’s creation.
It was a secret Rex still kept from himself.
The moment Xerollion’s energy touched the storm, the vortex didn’t explode; it unraveled. The lightning turned to harmless static; the wind collapsed into a harmless sigh.
FIIIIIIIIIIII SHHHH.
The magnificent column of destruction dissolved into glittering, harmless sparks that rained down like dying stars.
"You built that from nothing," Xerollion said, his voice cutting through the fading echoes of the storm. "You reached beyond your programming to find something new."
"I’m almost impressed... Almost."
Rex Rexilion staggered. For the first time since the confrontation began, the construct showed a visible crack in its heroic facade.
Its shoulders slumped fractionally, its head tilted in a moment of genuine, programmed uncertainty. It was the first time the ’hero’ looked uncertain.
Xerollion didn’t grant it mercy. He didn’t grant it a moment to think.
WHAM! CRUNCH! THUD!
He closed the distance like a predator closing on wounded prey. He unleashed a brutal three-strike combination with terrifying economy of motion.
First, a piston-like punch to the stomach that made the construct’s midsection buckle with a wet OOF, forcing a spray of synthetic blood from its lips.
Second, a vicious left hook that snapped Rex’s jaw sideways with a bone-deep CLACK.
And third, a devastating sweeping kick that hooked behind the construct’s ankles.
CRASH!!!
Rex hit the stone floor hard, sending up a choking cloud of pulverized masonry and dust. For several seconds, the construct simply lay there.
Its chest rose and fell in a labored rhythm that mimicked human exhaustion with such unsettling accuracy that it felt more like watching a dying man than a failing machine.
A ripple of horrified silence swept through the Aethelgard soldiers. The hope that had been building the belief that their savior was winning was dying a painful death.
Near the back, the young soldier who had whispered her certainty earlier now stood frozen, both hands pressed to her mouth, her eyes widening as her hope curdled into raw, nauseating despair.
But Rex Rexilion was not programmed to accept defeat.
GRRRR KRAK!
With a sound like grinding metal, the construct forced itself back up. It didn’t stand with dignity; it rose with the stubborn, suicidal refusal to stay down that had defined Rex’s entire legend.
It abandoned the graceful choreography of his combat style. It abandoned the precision.
It became something primal.
WHACK! WHACK! WHACK! WHACK!
Rex launched into a wild, desperate flurry of blows. It was a storm of raw volume overlapping bursts of flame, jagged ice shards, and compressed telekinetic strikes thrown in rapid succession.
He wasn’t fighting to win anymore; he was fighting to exist. Every strike was a scream of defiance, a chaotic mess of energy that lacked technique but possessed terrifying momentum.

Xerollion moved through the chaos like a ghost walking through rain. He ducked a flaming fist, spun under a telekinetic wave, and stepped aside from a shard of ice, all with an eerie, effortless grace that made the gap between their skill levels unmistakable.

"That’s closer to honest than anything you’ve shown me yet," Xerollion said, his voice calm even as the shockwaves of the construct’s attacks buffeted his cloak. "Desperation doesn’t need a dataset to improvise with..."
"It doesn’t need logic."
He ducked beneath a wild swing, his eyes gleaming with cruel satisfaction.
"Shame it took you this long to find it."
"Now that you’ve found your desperation... let’s see how long you can hold onto it."
Xerollion waited.
He didn’t counter; he didn’t retreat. He simply stood in the center of the elemental hurricane, letting the construct’s desperate, uncoordinated fury wash over him.
WHACK. THUD. SHHH BOOM.
His forearms took the brunt of the improvised strikes: fire-laced punches that left blackened burns and telekinetic impacts that threatened to shatter bone.
But each time the flesh split or the bone groaned under the stress, the wound sealed with an obscene, wet SQUELCH, knitting itself back together before the blood could even drip.
He let the flurry exhaust itself. He watched with cold, analytical fascination as the construct’s movements began to stutter.
The simulated breathing became ragged, wet gasps; the arms began to tremble with a simulated exhaustion so perfect it was almost nauseating.
The construct’s systems had decided to mimic the exact moment of human collapse, and Xerollion was more than happy to oblige.
The moment the construct’s guard wavered, the moment its next strike became a sluggish, desperate lunge, Xerollion moved.
SHHH FWOOM!

He stepped inside the guard with lethal precision, closing the distance before the construct could even register his movement. His palm struck the construct’s sternum with the force of a falling star.
KRA BOOOOOM!!!

The impact didn’t just send a shockwave through the construct; it sent a shockwave through the very foundation of the corridor. The stone floor beneath them shattered into a spiderweb of lethal shrapnel.
WHAM!!!
Rex Rexilion was launched backward like a broken doll. His body tore through the air until CRASH! he slammed into the remains of a massive, collapsed marble pillar.
The impact was catastrophic. The pillar groaned under the force, then surrendered, disintegrating in a thunderous cascade of debris.
CRUNCH. RUMBLE. SHATTER.
A mountain of broken rock and ancient dust swallowed the figure whole.
Silence fell. Not a peaceful silence, but a heavy, suffocating void that seemed to press against the eardrums of everyone present.
For several agonizing seconds, nobody moved. The Aethelgard soldiers stood like statues carved from grief, their eyes hollow.

The hope that had briefly ignited in them hadn’t just died; it had been executed. Several soldiers simply collapsed, their legs giving out as they sank to their knees in the rubble, their heads bowed in surrender to the inevitable.
Behind them, the Underlayer rebels held a different kind of breath. Cassandra’s fingers twitched, drifting toward the hilt of her blade with instinctive readiness.

Gorvasha’s jaw was set so hard it looked ready to crack, his entire body coiled like a spring, eyes tracking Xerollion with lethal calculation. They weren’t mourning; they were waiting for the signal to either die or kill.
TAP. TAP. TAP.
The sound of boots on stone echoed in the hollow corridor. Xerollion walked toward the wreckage.
He showed no urgency, no triumph, only a calm, almost contemplative curiosity. He approached the pile of debris as one might approach a fascinating specimen under a microscope.
As the dust settled, the broken form of Rex Rexilion became visible. He lay twisted across the jagged stones, limbs at unnatural angles, synthetic blood seeping from multiple wounds.
Yet, even there, amidst the ruin, the construct’s fingers twitched. A muscle in its neck spasmed. The faint, pathetic beginnings of an attempt to rise.
Xerollion reached the body and sank to one knee beside it. He didn’t loom; he crouched, bringing himself level with the dying echo.
His mask tilted downward, studying the fractured face of the hero.

TAP.
TAP.
TAP.
The sound of boots on stone echoed in the hollow corridor.
Xerollion walked toward the wreckage.
He showed no urgency, no triumph, only a calm, almost contemplative curiosity.
He approached the pile of debris as one might approach a fascinating specimen under a microscope.
As the dust settled, the broken form of Rex Rexilion became visible.
He lay twisted across the jagged stones, limbs at unnatural angles, synthetic blood seeping from multiple wounds.
Yet, even there, amidst the ruin, the construct’s fingers twitched.
A muscle in its neck spasmed.
The faint, pathetic beginnings of an attempt to rise.
Xerollion reached the body and sank to one knee beside it.
He didn’t loom; he crouched, bringing himself level with the dying echo.
His mask tilted downward, studying the fractured face of the hero.

chapters.title: Chapter 1209. Did You Really Think I Wouldn’t Know How to Use It Against You?
paragraphs: "You did better than I expected," Xerollion said softly.
His voice was intimate, almost tender, carrying only to the two of them like a secret shared between lovers in a graveyard. "Ninety seven point three percent... An extraordinary number."
"A masterpiece of behavioral fidelity."
He reached out, almost gently, and brushed a speck of stone dust from the construct’s forehead.

"I built you well, little echo... I truly did." A dark, satisfied smile played beneath his mask as he leaned closer, his breath ghosting over the construct’s face. "I just happen to be the other two point seven."
Rex Rexilion’s fingers scraped against the jagged debris, leaving faint trails in the stone dust. His hand twitched a weak, spasmodic curl of tendons, and his eyes cracked open halfway.
Through the haze of simulated agony, he fixed his gaze on the masked nightmare hovering above him.
In that moment, something flickered across the construct’s face—not quite a human emotion, but a ghost of it. A final, defiant spark of hatred that burned brighter than any programmed directive.
Xerollion didn’t flinch at the gaze. Instead, he raised one hand.
Between his fingers, violet black energy began to writhe like living smoke, coalescing into a sphere of concentrated annihilation.
VROOOOOM.
The air began to hum with a lethal, low-frequency vibration that made the teeth of every witness ache. Across the ruined corridor, every soldier still conscious held their breath.
They weren’t just watching a fight anymore; they were watching an execution.
But Rex Rexilion was not ready to die. His systems screamed for one last gambit, a desperate fusion of everything he had learned from his creator.
KRA KOOOOOM!!!
The ground beneath the construct didn’t just shake; it exploded upward. Rex channeled Earthen Divine Authority, forcing the very bones of the corridor to reshape themselves.
A massive stone golem, three times the height of a man and rough hewn from the foundation itself, tore free from the floor in a shower of gravel and ancient mortar.
RUMBLE SHHHH!
Simultaneously, the construct’s other hand clawed at the air, channeling Sovereign Necromancy. The effect was instantaneous and horrific.

From the scattered remains of soldiers fallen earlier in the siege, corpses began to twitch. Bone scraped against stone as they dragged themselves upright, their movements slack and purposeless, their eyes empty sockets animated by necromantic threads.
CLACK. DRAG. SHUFFLE.

For three terrifying seconds, the tactical calculus shifted. Three independent threats—the towering golem, the reanimated dead from the left, and the shambling horrors from the right—converged on Xerollion at once.
Even Xerollion’s god-like focus was forced to fracture.
"You dare... use my own filth against me?" Xerollion hissed, his voice distorted by the gathering energy.
The golem’s first swing came down like a guillotine.
WHAM!!!
Xerollion rolled sideways just as the fist struck, the impact sending a shockwave through the corridor that split the floor into a spiderweb of fresh, lethal cracks.
CRACK THUD.
Xerollion began to rise, but he was too slow. The nearest corpse had already closed the distance with unnatural speed, its cold, dead fingers locking around his ankle like a vice.
GRIP.
The necromantic energy coursing through the corpse gave it strength beyond what flesh should possess.
Xerollion’s balance wavered. His heel slipped on the loose debris.
WHOOSH CRUNCH!!!
The golem’s second swing didn’t graze him. It found him.
The massive stone fist connected squarely with Xerollion’s ribs as he was off balance, the sound of the impact echoing like a cannon shot through the chamber.
KRA A AACK!
The force sent him crashing sideways into a wall, the stone behind him spiderwebbing from the blow.
The chaos was absolute. For the first time in his existence, Xerollion was not the one orchestrating the symphony of violence; he was drowning in it.
KRA THOOOM!

The golem’s massive fist slammed into his shoulder while his focus was momentarily fractured by the necromantic tether around his ankle. The sound was sickening—the wet CRUNCH of cartilage and bone grinding beneath the supernatural force.
Xerollion grunted, the pain a foreign but sharp stimulus that cut through his usual detachment. But he had no time to compensate.
In the split second of vulnerability created by that distraction, the construct Rex Rexilion lunged forward.
WHACK!
A follow-up strike, precise and vicious, caught Xerollion across the jaw. His head snapped sideways with enough force to make his vision blur into static.
SHHH...!
A fresh crimson line split open along his cheekbone as blood sprayed across his mask, warm and metallic.
"Impressive... truly," Xerollion hissed through clenched teeth, though his inner mind was racing, recalculating variables at lightning speed.
’Target acquisition compromised.’
’Defensive protocols failing.’
’Need to sever the threads immediately.’
A second corpse, a former Aethelgard captain with hollow eyes, clawed at his other side, its teeth gnashing in a silent, undead hunger.
Xerollion didn’t waste motion trying to pry the dead fingers off. Instead, he channeled a burst of kinetic energy through his leg and drove his knee upward.
CRUNCH SQUELCH!
His knee connected with the corpse’s sternum with the force of a battering ram. The ribcage collapsed inward like dried kindling, the chest cavity caving in with a wet, splintering sound.

The body crumpled to the floor, a broken husk, but the necromantic threads were stubborn; even as the corpse lay motionless, its fingers continued to twitch uselessly against the stone in a macabre parody of life.
TAP. TAP. SCRAPE.
The golem pressed forward, its massive weight causing the corridor to groan.
GRRRRIND.
Each step it took dragged a foot through the rubble, creating a grinding scrape that sent showers of dust and pebbles raining down from the cracked ceiling.
SHHHHHHH.
It swung a third time a low, devastating horizontal sweep aimed directly at Xerollion’s ribs.
BOOM!
Xerollion crossed his forearms to block, but the sheer mass behind the blow was overwhelming. The impact drove him backward, his boots skidding across the debris as he fought to maintain his footing.
The stone beneath his heels shattered under the pressure of his resistance.
CRACKLE.
"You taught me how to raise the dead," the construct spoke.
The voice was chilling. It wasn’t the mechanical drone of a machine; it carried the exact timbre, the exact unshakable conviction, the exact heroic resonance of the real Rex Rexilion.
It was a weaponized echo of a soul. "Did you really think I wouldn’t know how to use it against you?"
Xerollion’s eyes narrowed behind his mask. The golem’s massive hand was already reaching out, its stone fingers poised to crush his throat.
VROOOOM SHATTER!
With a sudden, violent flick of his wrist, Xerollion unleashed a concentrated telekinetic pulse. The golem’s reaching hand didn’t just stop it; it exploded.
Stone fragments flew in every direction like shrapnel as the limb was pulverized before it could make contact.
KRAK CHHH!
Xerollion straightened his spine, blood dripping from his split cheek onto the ruined floor, his violet black energy flaring brighter than before.
"I did think that," Xerollion admitted, his voice dropping to a dangerous, purring register. "I anticipated the move, the timing, even the desperation."
"I accounted for everything."
He stepped forward, the ground cracking beneath his renewed magical pressure.
"Right up until you actually did it..."
"Credit where it’s owed, little echo."
