"Afraid that I would see the monster the world had made her and realize I was responsible for letting it happen."

She spoke of Celestina’s growing resentment of how the girl had watched the reincarnator system corrupt the natural order of Erosyne, seeing it as a cancerous cycle that denied souls their true purpose.
She laid bare the trauma of their separation, the wound that had never closed, the resentment that had festered into a crusade.
Xerollion listened with the terrifying patience of a statue.
He nodded slowly, the motion almost imperceptible, as if he were merely checking off items on a list.
In his mind, he was already weaving Celestina’s trauma into a weapon, calculating how her crusade against reincarnation could be manipulated to serve his own dominion.

There was a faint, private irony beneath his mask, a stillness that Valentina was too broken to interpret, but it was there: the unnerving calm of a man confirming a truth he had already heard once before, years earlier, from those same lips in a room that no longer existed.
The silence that followed was worse than the confession.
It was the silence of a predator who had finished feeding on a memory and was now ready to strike at the living.
"One more thing," Xerollion said.
The shift in his tone was subtle, but it felt like the click of a crossbow trigger.
"Helena...
Your daughter.
"She still hasn’t returned from her mission with Leonidas."
The effect was instantaneous.
Valentina’s head snapped up, the grief in her eyes replaced by a sharp, piercing terror, the raw, primal fear of a mother.
For a moment, the headmaster vanished, leaving only a woman clinging to the last thread of hope she possessed.
Her hands gripped the desk so hard the wood groaned under her touch.
"She’ll be home soon," Valentina said.
She forced her voice to steady, summoning every ounce of maternal conviction she could muster.
"Her last letter was clear...
Their mission is nearly complete."
"She is capable, Xerollion...
She is strong."
"Perhaps within the next few weeks, she will return to Aethelgard."
She spoke with a desperate certainty, as if her words alone could summon her daughter back from whatever darkness she had wandered into.
Xerollion didn’t offer reassurance.
He didn’t offer comfort.
He simply met her gaze with those cold, unreadable eyes behind the mask, and the words he spoke next felt like a promise of inevitable doom.
"Good," Xerollion said.
"I want to meet her the moment she returns."
A silence more profound than the one before descended upon the room, but this was not the silence of exhaustion; it was the silence of an approaching storm.
Valentina stared at him, her pulse hammering against her throat like a trapped bird.
Every instinct she possessed, every defensive spell woven into her very marrow, screamed at her.
’Why?’ The question burned in her mind.
Why would a conqueror, a being who had just systematically dismantled a kingdom, express interest in a young commander who was still leagues away?
Was she being baited?
Was Helena a hostage she hadn’t even realized she’d lost?
The wariness in her eyes sharpened into something dangerous, something almost desperate.
"What interest could you possibly have in my daughter?" she demanded, her voice cracking with restrained fury.
"She is not a pawn in your game of thrones, Xerollion."
Xerollion did not answer immediately.
Instead, he performed an action so alien to his predatory persona that it froze the very air in Valentina’s lungs.
Slowly, deliberately, he raised one gauntleted hand to the edge of his mask.

"Before that," he said, his voice carrying a strange, almost nostalgic cadence that made the hair on Valentina’s neck stand on end, "I think you deserve to know exactly who you’ve actually been speaking with."
The mask didn’t simply fall off.
It dissolved.
Valentina watched in horrified fascination as the pulsing, violet-black energy that had formed the impenetrable visor began to liquefy.
The shadowy substance writhed like living smoke, bleeding back into his skin, flowing into his pores in tendrils of malevolent light.
As the darkness receded, the face beneath was revealed.
Valentina’s heart didn’t just skip a beat; it seemed to stop entirely.
The face was achingly familiar.
It was a face she had seen in countless commendations, a face that had graced the stained glass of the Grand Academy’s hall, a face she had personally guided, mentored, and praised.
It was the face of the boy who had been the academy’s brightest star, the prodigy who had shown more promise than any student in three centuries.
The hero who had stood at the front lines of every crisis, the one she had trusted with the innermost secrets of Aethelgard’s defenses.
The one she had considered a son in all but blood.
Rex.
Rexilion.
"No..." The word was barely a breath, a sound of pure, unadulterated agony.
"No, it can’t be..."
Valentina’s composure didn’t just crack; it shattered like glass under a warhammer.
Her eyes widened with such violent shock that the muscles in her face seemed to spasm.
Her chair shrieked against the marble floor screeeeeeeee as she lurched backward, rising reflexively from her desk as if the very air around her had become poisonous.
The chair toppled, clattering to the ground behind her, but she didn’t notice.
Her entire world began to collapse inward.
The devastating arithmetic of the last few hours began to rearrange itself with terrifying speed behind her eyes.
The surrender wasn’t just a defeat; it was a betrayal.
The speech in the plaza hadn’t been a tyrant’s monologue; it had been a performance.
And her confession, her raw, bleeding vulnerability about Celestina, about her deepest shames and her most guarded secrets, hadn’t been given to a monster.
It had been fed, piece by piece, to the one person she thought would have died to protect her.
Every word she had spoken, every strategic weakness she had revealed, every vulnerability she had exposed in her moment of weakness... she had handed them all to the wolf she had raised herself.
She stared at him at Rex and saw not the hero of Aethelgard, but the architect of its annihilation.

chapters.title: Chapter 1226. They Are Not Two Different People, Just Two Sides of the Same Truth
paragraphs: "No," Valentina whispered.
The word was fragile, a splinter of glass breaking in the hollow of her throat. "No... that isn’t possible."

"You’re... you’re Rex." Her mind scrambled, clawing at the memories of a boy who had stood before her in the courtyard, whose potential had burned brighter than any candle in the archives. "You’re the student of this academy..."
"You’re the one who saved the eastern gate from the rift... You’re the one who—"
"I am all of those things, Valentina."
Rex cut her off. His voice wasn’t the warm, respectful tone of the prodigy she remembered.
It was something colder, something ancient, a voice that had seen empires crumble and found the experience amusing.
He didn’t flinch at her accusation; he didn’t even blink. The boyish softness she had once seen in his eyes had been replaced by a terrifying, bottomless void.
"I am Tremor," he continued, each name dropping like a guillotine blade. "I am Lord Xerollion..."
"I am the Undead Bringer who walked through the ashes of the fallen."

"And I am... Rex Rexilion." He took a single step forward, the marble floor beneath his boot cracking with a spiderweb of fractures as if the earth itself recoiled from his presence. "All of it is me."
"All along..."
"The hero you saw, and the monster you fear..."
"They are not two different people, Valentina... They are simply two sides of the same inevitable truth."
The revelation hit her with the force of a physical cataclysm. Her breathing became shallow, ragged gasps that sounded like tearing parchment.
’He was there,’ her mind screamed. ’When Apollo fell, when the screams filled the streets and the sky turned crimson with blood, he was there.’
’He wasn’t fighting the enemy; he was watching.’
’He was studying us. He was harvesting our despair.’
The betrayal wasn’t just a sting; it was a poison that flooded her veins, turning her grief into something molten and volatile.

The shock passed, burned away by a white-hot fury that consumed every remaining spark of her exhausted consciousness. Every lesson she had taught him, every moment of trust she had invested in him, felt like a blade twisted in her own gut.
"YOU KILLED APOLLO!" Valentina screamed.
The sound that tore from her throat was primal, inhuman—the shriek of a mother losing everything. She didn’t just attack; she exploded.
With a desperate, convulsive motion of her hands, she tore at the very fabric of the ambient mana in the room.
The magical energy she had been hoarding, the residual power from her failed defenses, coalesced around her palms in a chaotic, unstable sphere of blinding white light.
CRACK BOOM!
The air itself seemed to shatter as she unleashed a torrent of raw, unfiltered spellwork.
"YOU DESTROYED MY CITY!" she shrieked again, her voice cracking as she poured her hatred into the magical assault. "You watched them die!
"You watched the children scream, you watched the buildings collapse, and you did nothing but smile behind that mask!"
The spell streaked across the office like a comet of pure rage. The desk was vaporized instantly, splinters of enchanted obsidian flying through the air like shrapnel.
The windows exploded outward in a cascade of glittering shards as the shockwave tore through the room.

"YOU LIED TO ALL OF US THIS ENTIRE TIME!" Valentina roared, her eyes bloodshot, tears streaming down her face as she charged toward him, her hands glowing with enough energy to level the tower. "You played us like puppets!"
"You sat at our tables, you ate our food, and you took our praise, all while you were measuring our throats for the blade!"
"How can you stand there?!"
"How can you have the nerve to sit here in front of me with the same face we all trusted the face of a son while you carry the stench of our corpses on your hands!?"

Her magical aura flared violently, casting monstrous, dancing shadows against the walls as she prepared to unleash everything she had left, her entire existence reduced to a single, desperate need to break the boy who had broken her world.
The spell arrived with the fury of a dying star, a compressed bolt of white fire, screaming through the air as it tore at the very oxygen in the room.
It was a desperate, suicidal casting, the kind of forbidden technique Valentina would have condemned in any student, but now she threw it at him with everything she was.
She poured every ounce of her grief, her rage, and her shattered hope into that single arc of light.
WHOOOOOM.
But the expected explosion never came.
Rex didn’t dodge. He didn’t raise a shield.
He simply reached out with one hand. His fingers closed around the bolt of white fire as if it were nothing more than a stray ember.
The magical torrent hissed violently, sparks cascading off his palm like water hitting hot iron, before it collapsed in on itself, imploding into nothingness against his skin.
His sleeve remained unburned; his skin remained unblemished. The silence that followed was deafening, broken only by the ragged, wet sound of Valentina’s breathing.

Her mouth remained frozen open around the unfinished syllable of her scream. Her eyes, wide and bloodshot, fixed on his palm—the palm she had once seen pat a grateful student on the shoulder, now the hand that had just swallowed her last desperate hope.
’It’s impossible,’ her mind shrieked. ’He’s not human. He’s not even... he’s not Rex anymore.’
The shock lasted only a heartbeat before it curdled into something darker. She couldn’t use magic. She couldn’t think.
There was only the animal. There was only the need to feel his bones crack beneath her touch.

Abandoning all dignity, all technique, and all the centuries of refined arcane discipline, Valentina lunged. She threw herself at him with a raw, clawed swipe aimed directly at his eyes, a desperate, murderous lunge born of pure, unadulterated psychosis.
Swish THUD.
Rex caught her wrist mid swing. He didn’t even brace himself.
He caught her with the casual, bored precision of a man catching a falling quill. Valentina’s entire body lurched to a halt, her bones grinding against the sudden stop.
She began to thrash, her free hand scrabbling at his chest, her feet kicking uselessly against his shins as she screamed curses that sounded more like whimpers.
"Enough."
The word wasn’t shouted; it was spoken with the flat finality of a closing tomb. Without warning, Rex drove his free fist into her solar plexus.
CRUNCH.
The sound was wet and sickening, the unmistakable noise of cartilage compressing and ribs bowing under impossible force.
Valentina’s breath didn’t just leave her; it was violently evicted. Her lungs seized, her diaphragm spasming in agony as she was hurled backward.
She staggered, her legs folding like wet paper, before she collapsed onto the cold marble floor of her own office.
Hack cough wheeze.
She lay there, curled in a fetal position, retching up flecks of crimson blood that spattered across the pristine stones. Her vision swam in kaleidoscopic patterns of pain.
Through the haze of agony, she saw his boots approaching. Slow and deliberate.
Each step sounded like a hammer striking an anvil in the silence of her ruined sanctuary.
She tried to crawl. Her fingernails scraped against the stone, skreeeeee, skreeeeee leaving bloody furrows as she attempted to push herself upright.
"Get... away..." she gasped, her voice a broken rasp. "You... monster..."
Before she could gain purchase, a fist tangled in her hair. Rex grabbed her by the scalp, yanking her head back with such brutal force that her neck vertebrae popped audibly.
Crack.
He forced her face upward, dragging her gaze from the floor to meet his.
Valentina looked into the eyes of the boy she had loved like a son, and she saw only a predator looking at prey. There was no recognition.
No remorse.
Just the terrifying, hollow emptiness of an abyss.
"Listen to me carefully, Valentina," Rex said, his voice dropping to a low, dangerous purr that made her blood run cold. "You’re fighting for a ghost."
"You’ve already watched what happened to Apollo..."
"You watched what happened to Elliot..."
"You saw Evelyn burn... And you saw yourself broken mere hours ago."
He leaned closer, his breath warm against her tear-stained cheek, contrasting horrifyingly with the ice in his voice.
"Look around you, Headmaster."
"Look at the ruins of everything you built..."
"You don’t have a single option left."

chapters.title: Chapter 1227. Death Is a Mercy, and I Am Not Feeling Merciful Today
paragraphs: Rex abruptly released his grip. Valentina fell backward like a broken marionette, her head snapping against the marble with a dull thud.

She lay there, convulsing slightly as her body struggled to process the agony in her ribs and the violation of her scalp. Her breathing was a wet, rattling, sound hiss wheeze as blood from her split lip smeared across her chin.
Her eyes, swollen and bloodshot, fixed on him with a cocktail of hatred so potent it should have burned, but beneath that rage lay something far more terrifying: a cold, paralyzing realization.
She was utterly, completely powerless.
Rex didn’t move to finish her. He simply stood over her, the shadow of his frame swallowing her whole, casting her into darkness.
When he spoke again, his voice was devoid of any inflection, as flat and unyielding as a tombstone.
"From now on," Rex said, each word precise, cutting through the silence like a scalpel, "you will do exactly as I command."
"You will be my eyes and ears..."
"You will gather every scrap of intelligence regarding the territories beyond Aethelgard."
"You will maintain absolute compliance within these walls... No riots, no hidden rebellions, and no pathetic attempts at martyrdom."

He paused, leaning down slightly, his shadow stretching across her broken form. "And most importantly, Valentina... you will make certain that when Helena returns, she does nothing foolish enough to force my hand."
"If she returns as a hero, she lives."
"If she returns as an obstacle..." He let the implication hang in the air like the smell of gunpowder. "I will make you watch as I break her, piece by agonizing piece, before you die."
A strangled sob escaped Valentina’s throat. The threat to Helena was the final killing blow. It wasn’t a physical wound; it was a spiritual evisceration.

Her daughter... her last hope, her last connection to a world that wasn’t broken was now nothing more than a leash wrapped around her throat. Her mind raced through impossible scenarios, searching for an escape, a hidden spell, or a last resort.
But there was nothing. The mana in the room felt dead, drained by his presence.
Her city was a corpse, her students were ghosts, and her daughter was a hostage to a boy she had once taught to love.
"You’re... a monster," Valentina whispered.
The words were weak, stripped of their authority, dissolving into a broken rasp that barely carried across the distance between them.
"Perhaps." Rex crouched down one last time, bringing his face level with hers.
Up close, there was no trace of the boy who used to ask for extra study hours. There was no Rex Rexilion here. There was only the architect of ruin.

"But I am the monster who holds your city’s fate, your family’s legacy, and your very soul in the palm of my hand." His eyes locked onto hers, pupils dilated, dark and bottomless. "So I suggest you stop mourning the past and start adapting to the future, Valentina."
"Because this isn’t the end of the war... This is merely the opening gambit."
He rose to his full height in one fluid, effortless motion. The scrape of his boots against the marble sounded like a final judgment.
Without another word, without so much as a glance at the destruction he had wrought, he turned his back on her.
Valentina remained on the floor, a broken woman in a ruined sanctuary. She watched his retreating figure, her vision blurring with fresh tears that burned like acid.
The betrayal was a wound that would never scab over; it was a poison that would seep into every memory she held dear.
Every smile he had given her, every ’thank you, Headmaster,’ every moment of shared triumph—all of it was now tainted, revealed as the calculated lies of a predator playing at being prey.
Rex walked out of the office with the same calm, measured stride he had always maintained as the Academy’s golden boy. The mask of civility was back in place, smooth and impenetrable.
As the heavy doors groaned shut behind him, he didn’t look back at the wreckage. His mind was already moving past Aethelgard, past the Underlayer, past the petty squabbles of kingdoms.
His gaze was fixed on the horizon of Erosyne itself, a vast, beautiful world that was about to learn exactly what happens when the hero decides to become the god of its destruction.
The heavy doors had barely settled into their frames when Rex paused in the corridor. His footsteps echoed in the empty hallway—click, click, click—a steady rhythm that suddenly faltered.
A cold, predatory thought crystallized in his mind, sharper than any blade. He had been too efficient. Too clinical.

He had broken her bones and her authority, but he hadn’t yet broken her spirit. A broken body could still harbor a spark of defiance; a broken mind, however, was something he could mold into whatever shape he desired.
To truly own Aethelgard, he couldn’t just rule it from a throne; he had to consume its heart. And Valentina was that heart.
"No," he murmured to the empty air, a dark smile tugging at the corner of his lips. "I left her with too much dignity intact."
He turned on his heel, his cape swirling behind him like a shroud as he stormed back toward the office. He didn’t knock.
He kicked the door open with such force that the ancient oak splintered at the hinges, CRACK BOOM, sending debris skittering across the marble where Valentina lay gasping.
Valentina flinched, her eyes widening in terror as she saw the shadow fall over her again.
"What... what more do you want?" she wheezed, clutching her bleeding ribs. "Kill me then... Just finish it."
"Kill you?" Rex’s laughter was soft, terrifyingly intimate.
He walked to her, his boots crunching on the glass shards of her shattered windows. "Death is a mercy, Valentina... And I am not feeling merciful today."
He reached down, grabbing her chin once more, forcing her to look at him. "My first command is not about intelligence gathering or city compliance."
"My first command is personal... You will come with me to the Starlight household."
"And there, you will submit to me completely... body, soul, and every inch of your flesh."
Valentina’s breath hitched. A different kind of horror washed over her, one that made the physical pain feel distant.
"What... what are you saying?"
"I am saying you will be my slave," Rex whispered, his voice dripping with venomous satisfaction. "You will be my fucktoy."
"You will learn to crave the very hands that crushed your ribs."
"You will learn that your only purpose now is to serve my pleasure."
"Never," she spat, a final, pathetic spark of defiance flickering in her eyes. "I would rather die—
"You think you have a choice?" Rex’s eyes suddenly glowed with an unnatural, pulsing violet light. "You think your ’will’ matters?"
Before she could blink, Rex activated his power. The air around them didn’t just distort; it tore. Time slowed to a glacial crawl, then fractured entirely.
He reached into the chronal stream, seizing a thread of possibility and dragging it into the present.
"Look, Valentina," he commanded, his voice echoing as if from another dimension. "Look at the price of your defiance."
A psychic shockwave erupted from Rex, flooding Valentina’s consciousness. She didn’t just see images; she lived them.
Through the manipulation of time, he forced her mind to experience a cascade of horrific futures.
’First came Lily.’ Valentina screamed as she felt the phantom sensation of her granddaughter’s throat being crushed beneath Rex’s boot.
She saw Lily’s eyes go dull, her lifeblood pooling on the floor while Rex watched with detached curiosity.
SQUELCH.

’Then came Diana.’ She felt the searing heat of magical fire consuming Diana’s flesh, the smell of burning hair and meat filling her nostrils as she watched her friend scream for a salvation that would never come.
’Then Elliot,’ the boy she had mentored.
She felt the wet snap of his spine as Rex tore him apart like a ragdoll, the sound of breaking bone reverberating in her own skull.
CRACK CRUNCH.
’Finally, Helena and Elizabeth...’ The vision focused on her daughter.
Valentina watched in helpless agony as Rex systematically dismantled Helena’s life, leaving her a broken, hollow shell before finally extinguishing her light.
The visions snapped shut like a trap. Valentina collapsed into a convulsion, her body wracked with violent tremors.
Blood leaked from her nose and ears as her brain struggled to process the temporal trauma. She was hyperventilating, her eyes rolling back in her head as she clawed at the floor.

"That is the future you choose if you resist me," Rex said, looming over her like a vengeful god. "Every time you deny me, every time you try to plot against me, I will show you another way to die..."
"I will show you every scream, every drop of blood, every moment of agony your loved ones will endure because of your stubbornness."
He leaned down, his lips brushing against her ear as she wept hysterically. "So, now you understand, don’t you?"
"You will come to the Starlight household. You will take whatever I give you."
"You will let me use you until there is nothing left of the headmaster but a hollow vessel for my desires."
"Because if you don’t... I will make those visions real."
Valentina couldn’t speak. She couldn’t even cry anymore; her tear ducts were spent.
She simply lay there, shaking uncontrollably, the images of her dead family seared into her retinas. The terror was absolute.
The hopelessness was total. She was no longer a woman, no longer a leader; she was merely prey waiting for the slaughter to begin.

sentences.text: Rex abruptly released his grip.
Valentina fell backward like a broken marionette, her head snapping against the marble with a dull thud.
She lay there, convulsing slightly as her body struggled to process the agony in her ribs and the violation of her scalp.
Her breathing was a wet, rattling, sound hiss wheeze as blood from her split lip smeared across her chin.
Her eyes, swollen and bloodshot, fixed on him with a cocktail of hatred so potent it should have burned, but beneath that rage lay something far more terrifying: a cold, paralyzing realization.
She was utterly, completely powerless.
Rex didn’t move to finish her.
He simply stood over her, the shadow of his frame swallowing her whole, casting her into darkness.
When he spoke again, his voice was devoid of any inflection, as flat and unyielding as a tombstone.
"From now on," Rex said, each word precise, cutting through the silence like a scalpel, "you will do exactly as I command."
"You will be my eyes and ears..."
"You will gather every scrap of intelligence regarding the territories beyond Aethelgard."
"You will maintain absolute compliance within these walls...
No riots, no hidden rebellions, and no pathetic attempts at martyrdom."
He paused, leaning down slightly, his shadow stretching across her broken form.
"And most importantly, Valentina... you will make certain that when Helena returns, she does nothing foolish enough to force my hand."
"If she returns as a hero, she lives."
"If she returns as an obstacle..." He let the implication hang in the air like the smell of gunpowder.
"I will make you watch as I break her, piece by agonizing piece, before you die."
A strangled sob escaped Valentina’s throat.
The threat to Helena was the final killing blow.
It wasn’t a physical wound; it was a spiritual evisceration.
Her daughter... her last hope, her last connection to a world that wasn’t broken was now nothing more than a leash wrapped around her throat.
Her mind raced through impossible scenarios, searching for an escape, a hidden spell, or a last resort.
But there was nothing.
The mana in the room felt dead, drained by his presence.
Her city was a corpse, her students were ghosts, and her daughter was a hostage to a boy she had once taught to love.
"You’re... a monster," Valentina whispered.
The words were weak, stripped of their authority, dissolving into a broken rasp that barely carried across the distance between them.
"Perhaps." Rex crouched down one last time, bringing his face level with hers.
Up close, there was no trace of the boy who used to ask for extra study hours.
There was no Rex Rexilion here.
There was only the architect of ruin.
"But I am the monster who holds your city’s fate, your family’s legacy, and your very soul in the palm of my hand." His eyes locked onto hers, pupils dilated, dark and bottomless.
"So I suggest you stop mourning the past and start adapting to the future, Valentina."
"Because this isn’t the end of the war...
This is merely the opening gambit."
He rose to his full height in one fluid, effortless motion.
The scrape of his boots against the marble sounded like a final judgment.
Without another word, without so much as a glance at the destruction he had wrought, he turned his back on her.
Valentina remained on the floor, a broken woman in a ruined sanctuary.
She watched his retreating figure, her vision blurring with fresh tears that burned like acid.
The betrayal was a wound that would never scab over; it was a poison that would seep into every memory she held dear.
Every smile he had given her, every ’thank you, Headmaster,’ every moment of shared triumph—all of it was now tainted, revealed as the calculated lies of a predator playing at being prey.
Rex walked out of the office with the same calm, measured stride he had always maintained as the Academy’s golden boy.
The mask of civility was back in place, smooth and impenetrable.
As the heavy doors groaned shut behind him, he didn’t look back at the wreckage.
His mind was already moving past Aethelgard, past the Underlayer, past the petty squabbles of kingdoms.
His gaze was fixed on the horizon of Erosyne itself, a vast, beautiful world that was about to learn exactly what happens when the hero decides to become the god of its destruction.
The heavy doors had barely settled into their frames when Rex paused in the corridor.
His footsteps echoed in the empty hallway—click, click, click—a steady rhythm that suddenly faltered.
A cold, predatory thought crystallized in his mind, sharper than any blade.
He had been too efficient.
Too clinical.
He had broken her bones and her authority, but he hadn’t yet broken her spirit.
A broken body could still harbor a spark of defiance; a broken mind, however, was something he could mold into whatever shape he desired.
To truly own Aethelgard, he couldn’t just rule it from a throne; he had to consume its heart.
And Valentina was that heart.
"No," he murmured to the empty air, a dark smile tugging at the corner of his lips.
"I left her with too much dignity intact."
He turned on his heel, his cape swirling behind him like a shroud as he stormed back toward the office.
He didn’t knock.
He kicked the door open with such force that the ancient oak splintered at the hinges, CRACK BOOM, sending debris skittering across the marble where Valentina lay gasping.
Valentina flinched, her eyes widening in terror as she saw the shadow fall over her again.
"What... what more do you want?" she wheezed, clutching her bleeding ribs.
"Kill me then...
Just finish it."
"Kill you?" Rex’s laughter was soft, terrifyingly intimate.
He walked to her, his boots crunching on the glass shards of her shattered windows.
"Death is a mercy, Valentina...
And I am not feeling merciful today."
He reached down, grabbing her chin once more, forcing her to look at him.
"My first command is not about intelligence gathering or city compliance."
"My first command is personal...
You will come with me to the Starlight household."
"And there, you will submit to me completely... body, soul, and every inch of your flesh."
Valentina’s breath hitched.
A different kind of horror washed over her, one that made the physical pain feel distant.
"What... what are you saying?"
"I am saying you will be my slave," Rex whispered, his voice dripping with venomous satisfaction.
"You will be my fucktoy."
"You will learn to crave the very hands that crushed your ribs."
"You will learn that your only purpose now is to serve my pleasure."
"Never," she spat, a final, pathetic spark of defiance flickering in her eyes.
"I would rather die—
"You think you have a choice?" Rex’s eyes suddenly glowed with an unnatural, pulsing violet light.
"You think your ’will’ matters?"
Before she could blink, Rex activated his power.
The air around them didn’t just distort; it tore.
Time slowed to a glacial crawl, then fractured entirely.
He reached into the chronal stream, seizing a thread of possibility and dragging it into the present.
"Look, Valentina," he commanded, his voice echoing as if from another dimension.
"Look at the price of your defiance."
A psychic shockwave erupted from Rex, flooding Valentina’s consciousness.
She didn’t just see images; she lived them.
Through the manipulation of time, he forced her mind to experience a cascade of horrific futures.
’First came Lily.’ Valentina screamed as she felt the phantom sensation of her granddaughter’s throat being crushed beneath Rex’s boot.
She saw Lily’s eyes go dull, her lifeblood pooling on the floor while Rex watched with detached curiosity.
SQUELCH.

’Then came Diana.’ She felt the searing heat of magical fire consuming Diana’s flesh, the smell of burning hair and meat filling her nostrils as she watched her friend scream for a salvation that would never come.
’Then Elliot,’ the boy she had mentored.
She felt the wet snap of his spine as Rex tore him apart like a ragdoll, the sound of breaking bone reverberating in her own skull.
CRACK CRUNCH.
’Finally, Helena and Elizabeth...’ The vision focused on her daughter.
Valentina watched in helpless agony as Rex systematically dismantled Helena’s life, leaving her a broken, hollow shell before finally extinguishing her light.
The visions snapped shut like a trap.
Valentina collapsed into a convulsion, her body wracked with violent tremors.
Blood leaked from her nose and ears as her brain struggled to process the temporal trauma.
She was hyperventilating, her eyes rolling back in her head as she clawed at the floor.
"That is the future you choose if you resist me," Rex said, looming over her like a vengeful god.
"Every time you deny me, every time you try to plot against me, I will show you another way to die..."
"I will show you every scream, every drop of blood, every moment of agony your loved ones will endure because of your stubbornness."
He leaned down, his lips brushing against her ear as she wept hysterically.
"So, now you understand, don’t you?"
"You will come to the Starlight household.
You will take whatever I give you."
"You will let me use you until there is nothing left of the headmaster but a hollow vessel for my desires."
"Because if you don’t...
I will make those visions real."
Valentina couldn’t speak.
She couldn’t even cry anymore; her tear ducts were spent.
She simply lay there, shaking uncontrollably, the images of her dead family seared into her retinas.
The terror was absolute.
The hopelessness was total.
She was no longer a woman, no longer a leader; she was merely prey waiting for the slaughter to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 1228. I Am Not Here to Be Their King. I Am Here to Be Their God
paragraphs: Valentina lay in the wreckage of her own life, her mind a shattered mirror reflecting only corpses and blood. The temporal visions Rex had forced upon her acted like acid, eating away at her sanity.

She could still feel the phantom sensation of Helena’s bones snapping; she could still hear the wet gurgle of Lily’s final breath. The trauma was so profound that her body began to reject itself, her muscles seizing in involuntary spasms.
’Please,’ her mind whispered, a broken, pathetic thing. ’Please, not them. Anything but them.’
"Please..." The word finally broke free from her lips, not as a command or a curse, but as a wet, desperate plea.
She dragged herself toward Rex’s boots, her fingernails leaving crimson streaks on the marble as she prostrated herself before him. "Stop... please stop showing me those things."
She looked up at him, her face a mask of agony, tears mixing with the blood streaming from her nose. "I’ll do it."
"I’ll give you... everything."
"My body, my dignity, my soul. Just... promise me."
"Promise me you won’t destroy Aethelgard."
"Promise you’ll spare them... Spare Helena... Spare the children..."
"I will be your slave, your toy; whatever you need, just keep your promise... Leave the city in peace."
She was bargaining with her own humanity, offering up her flesh as a sacrifice to appease a demon. She thought she had found the leverage.
She thought she had found the one thing a predator would respect: a transaction.
Rex stared down at her for a long moment. Then, the silence was broken by a sound that made Valentina’s blood run colder than any spell: laughter.
It wasn’t a villainous cackle; it was a genuine, amused chuckle, the kind a man might give when watching a child make an absurdly naive mistake.
"Oh, Valentina," Rex said, shaking his head as he looked down at her broken form. "You really are as naive as they said you were."
"Do you truly believe I need to bargain with you?"
The laughter died down, replaced by a smile that was sharp enough to draw blood. "You think I’m threatening Aethelgard to get what I want?"
"Valentina, you misunderstand my entire design."
"Aethelgard isn’t a target I’m trying to spare... Aethelgard is my first kingdom."
Valentina froze. The hope that had briefly flickered in her chest died instantly, replaced by a void of pure terror.
"What... what do you mean?"
"The Underlayer was merely a proving ground... A testing site for my power, a way to gather resources and test my methods," Rex said, stepping closer until his boot pressed against her wounded ribs.
He applied pressure just enough to make her gasp and retch blood onto the floor.
’Urrgh, huck.’
"But this city? This academy? This is where I will establish my throne... This is where my reign begins."
He knelt beside her, his fingers tracing the line of her jaw with terrifying tenderness. "I have no intention of destroying Aethelgard."
"I intend to rule it... I will bring order... I will bring peace..."
"But it will be a peace built on absolute submission. And you will be the foundation of that submission.
His eyes darkened with a hungry, predatory intent. "First, I break you."
"I use you until there is nothing left of the headmaster but a shell that exists only to serve my pleasure."
"Once you are properly broken, once you have learned to love the leash... then I will move on to Helena."
"And then Evelyn... I want them both."
"I want to see if their screams taste as sweet as yours."
Valentina’s heart hammered against her ribs like a trapped bird. "You’re... you’re insane."

"I am inevitable," Rex corrected. "And once I have claimed everything precious to you, once I have broken every pillar of resistance in this city, I will make Aethelgard the most stable kingdom in Erosyne."
"I will force the Underlayer to retreat... I will cleanse the corruption."
"I will be the savior this world deserves, but first, I will be the monster that owns it."
He grabbed her by the hair again, yanking her upright so she had to face the reality of her new existence. "Now, stand up..."
"We’re going to the Starlight household."
"We have work to do, and I find myself feeling... impatient."
As he dragged her toward the door, Valentina’s mind spiraled into darkness. She wasn’t saving her city; she was merely feeding the beast that was about to devour it.
She was the first offering in a ritual of conquest that would leave the entire world screaming her name.
The walk toward the exit felt like a march to the gallows. Valentina stumbled behind Rex, her legs shaking so violently she could barely maintain her balance.
Every step was agony; every breath felt like swallowing broken glass as her bruised ribs scraped against her lungs.
"Rex... please," she whimpered, her voice cracking. "Not like this... Not in front of the students... especially not in front of the guards."
"If you... if you truly intend to rule this city, you cannot show them this."
"They will see your cruelty... They will see you dragging their headmaster like common filth."
"Please, let us go privately... Let me dress; let me compose myself so you can maintain your image as their king."
It was a desperate gambit, an attempt to appeal to the cold logic of a conqueror. She hoped that by preserving his dignity, she might salvage a shred of her own.
Rex stopped abruptly. He didn’t turn around.
"You think I care about their perception?" His voice was hollow, amused. "I am not here to be their king, Valentina."
"I am here to be their god... And gods do not explain their movements to mortals."
Without warning, he grabbed her arm. His grip was like iron manacles. "But I appreciate your concern for my reputation."
"Very well. We shall avoid the eyes of the common rabble."
The world suddenly twisted. The air turned viscous, like water, and the space around them folded inward with a nauseating WHOOMP.

Valentina felt her stomach drop as if she were falling from a great height. Her vision blurred into streaks of violet and black as Rex’s teleportation magic tore through the fabric of reality, dragging them across the city in the blink of an eye.
When the world solidified again, the familiar, warm opulence of the Starlight household rushed back. But it felt wrong.
The air was too still, too heavy with an unnatural tension.
"Wait," Rex murmured, his eyes narrowing. "I want to ensure our... privacy is absolute."
Valentina’s heart froze. "Rex, no... Don’t—"
But he was already moving, dragging her toward the private wing of the mansion. Valentina watched through tear-blurred eyes as they crossed the threshold, her mind screaming.
’Not them. Please, not the children.’
They reached the inner sanctum, the door swinging open to reveal a scene that shattered Valentina’s remaining sanity more effectively than any temporal vision ever could.
Lily and Diana were there. But they weren’t frightened.
They weren’t screaming.
They were kneeling.
The two young girls, whose innocence Valentina had spent years protecting, were positioned at Rex’s feet like devoted acolytes.
Their eyes were glazed, pupils dilated in a way that spoke of a deep, chemical obsession. They looked up at Rex not with fear, but with a terrifying, hungry adoration.
"Rex..." Lily whispered, her voice unnaturally sweet, almost melodic. "You’re back."
"We waited for you," Diana added, her hands trembling with excitement as she reached out to touch the hem of his cloak.
Valentina felt the world tilt. "Lily? Diana?"
"What... what have you done to them?" she gasped, her voice breaking into a sob. "Run! Get away from him!"
But the girls didn’t move. Instead, they rose with fluid, practiced grace.

They moved toward Rex like moths to a flame. Valentina watched in horrified fascination as Lily leaned in, pressing a soft, reverent kiss to Rex’s cheek, while Diana took his other hand, pressing her lips to his knuckles.
’This is impossible,’ Valentina thought, her mind fracturing. ’This isn’t corruption. This is... devotion.’
’They love him. They love the monster.’
"We’ll leave you to your business, Rex," Lily said, casting a sidelong glance at Valentina.
There was no sympathy in her eyes, only a cold, unsettling pity. "We’ll be in the gardens, waiting for your next command."
"Don’t be too hard on Grandmother," Diana giggled, a sound that sent shivers of pure revulsion down Valentina’s spine. "She just needs to learn how to serve you properly, like we did."
With a synchronized bow that looked almost ritualistic, the two girls turned and walked away, their movements light and carefree, leaving behind a trail of shattered hope.
Valentina sank to her knees, her legs finally giving out. She watched them leave, knowing that the girls she loved were already lost to the abyss Rex had created.
They weren’t victims; they were converts. They had seen the power and tasted the inevitability, and they had chosen to kneel.
Rex turned his attention back to Valentina. The door clicked shut behind them, sealing them in the opulent silence of the Starlight household.
The last shred of Valentina’s resistance evaporated, leaving only the raw, exposed nerve of her terror.
"Now," Rex said, his voice dropping to that intimate, deadly purr as he loomed over her. "Finally... Just us."

chapters.title: Chapter 1229. I’m Going To Enjoy Breaking The Headmaster... By A Lot!
paragraphs: Valentina collapsed against the polished mahogany floor, her forehead pressed against the wood as she wept.

The sight of Lily and Diana, her precious, innocent girls, kissing the hands of her tormentor had severed something vital in her psyche. She was no longer fighting for her dignity; she was fighting for the remnants of her bloodline.
"Rex, please..." she croaked, her voice wet with blood and desperation. "I’ll do it..."
"I’ll give you everything... I will be whatever you want."
"I will let you destroy me, piece by piece, night after night, until there is nothing left of me but a husk."
"But please... spare them... Leave Lily, leave Diana, leave Helena and Elizabeth alone."
"Let them live their lives... Let them have their innocence!"
"Take all my suffering, all my pain, all my humiliation, but please... just leave them out of this."
She was offering herself as a human shield, a living sacrifice to buy back the souls of her children. It was the ultimate act of maternal martyrdom.
Rex didn’t respond with words. Instead, the air cracked with the sound of his movement.
SLAP.
The force of his palm connecting with her cheek sent her head spinning sideways. Her vision exploded in white sparks, and the metallic taste of blood flooded her mouth as her teeth split.
Before she could even process the shock, his fist came crashing into her jaw.
CRUNCH.
The sound of cartilage breaking was sickeningly loud in the quiet room. Valentina’s head snapped back, her body convulsing from the impact.
"Pathetic," Rex hissed.
He grabbed her by the hair, hauling her face up to meet his cold, impassive gaze. Valentina’s left eye was already swelling shut, purple and angry.
"You think you’re negotiating?" he asked, his voice dropping to a dangerous whisper. "You think your ’sacrifice’ matters to me?"
"You think I want a martyr?"
"I... I’ll do anything..." she gasped through a mouthful of blood.
"I know you will." Without warning, his hand glowed with a soft, sickly violet light.
He pressed it against her shattered jaw. Valentina screamed a raw, guttural sound of pure agony as she felt her bones knitting back together, her flesh sealing with an unnatural heat.
The pain was worse than the breaking; it was the sensation of being forcibly reconstructed, of being denied the mercy of death.
Within seconds, her face was flawless again. Her jaw was straight, her skin unblemished, her breathing steady.
He had healed her simply so he could break her again.
"There," Rex said, releasing her. "Now you’re ready."
His boot came down hard on her shoulder, pinning her to the floor. "Now, Valentina... Bow."
"I want to see the great headmaster of Aethelgard reduced to something proper."
"Please."
"BOW!" he roared, his voice echoing like thunder in the confined space.
Trembling, her spirit utterly broken by the cruelty of his ’mercy,’ Valentina lowered herself. She pressed her forehead against the cold marble, her body shaking with humiliating sobs.
She was no longer a queen, no longer a teacher; she was a worm beneath his boot.
Thud.
